# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

</system-reminder>

192	### Core Rules
193	
194	*Conventions.* Rules are named `PF-n`; each states a **Rule**, a **Why** and **Edge notes**. Formulas are `D.n` (Formulas section, written in part 2 of this document; the rules below fix *what* each formula must compute and its binding constants, and name it). Every pixel measure is in **art px of the 640x360 base picture**; on screen it is `k` times larger at integer zoom `k` in `[1, k_auto + 2]` (`k_auto = floor(min(W/640, H/360))`, PIPE PR-1, C6). Registry constants are cited by **name and registry value**; a number marked `[PLACEHOLDER]` is invented here, carries a range and a proposed registered name, and is final nowhere (reflexion: a placeholder never becomes a fact). Upstream facts are cited by rule id first (`SN-15 L-L`, `HE-40`). Anything about Accessibility Settings or Co-op Session is **(provisional — undesigned)**; HUD & Suit Layer, In-World Instruments & Inspect View, Debug Overlay (True Values) and Adaptive Audio & Tells have since been designed and their answers are recorded in Interactions I-B and OQ-PF-29 (2026-10-27 consistency pass). For the undesigned neighbours: this GDD places a requirement on the neighbour and describes what the Filter *returns*, never the neighbour's internals. There is no `scripting.md` or `core.md` in `docs/engine-reference/godot/`: GDScript integer-overflow, `Dictionary` ordering, `RefCounted` lifetime and per-call cost are **not sourceable** and are marked `[UNV]` wherever a rule depends on them; the reference also carries nothing on `canvas_item` shader instance parameters, container materials or viewport masking, so every shading-language mechanism is a `[UNV]` spike item, never the basis of a rule.
195	
196	#### A. Architecture, channels and the tag contract
197	
198	**PF-1. Channel architecture: consume, do not own.**
199	*Rule.* The Filter registers no kernel block, no step hook and no mutator (KERN CR-3, CR-8, CR-9). The `PERCEPTION_OUT` block of the routed thread is `sanity.perception`, which the Filter consumes. The Filter's **perceived channel** (the `Perceived` records, the lie trajectories, the per-viewer decoy list, the rim and outline state) is a presentation-side surface that inherits every `PERCEPTION_OUT` rule: no simulation system reads it (kernel H5), it is never persisted, it is never part of `state_hash` (KERN D.12). KERN C.3 row 11 grants the Filter "Subscriptions only ... Neither gets submit or mutators"; it subscribes as `PRESENTATION`.
200	*Why.* A `PRESENTATION` subscriber cannot write a block (H3, H4), and the kernel defines the class as Sanity's output. Stating the reading on page one keeps a reviewer from reading the thread literally.
201	*Edge notes.* Lighting's row says "a per-client `PERCEPTION_OUT` decoy list"; under this rule that list is a Filter-published presentation list (refresh row 20). -> ADR candidate: Filter channel architecture and the "no block" ruling. (orchestrator ruling R1.)
202	
203	**PF-2. Write set.**
204	*Rule.* The Filter writes `CanvasItem` members, `Material` and shader parameters (including per-instance parameters), particle members and audio *requests*. It writes **no member of any real light** (LO-25 (ii): "the Filter writes no `Light2D` member"), no `Camera2D`, `Viewport`, `SubViewport` or `SubViewportContainer` property (PIPE C1, C9; the container's `material` slot is assigned and nulled by the pipeline root, PF-25), no simulation state and no block. A grep-able lint enforces every clause (AC-PF-8).
205	*Why.* The true reveal radius is an anchor (EM-29); a Filter-written light member would be a path to move it. The six upstream clauses that still say "CanvasItem/Material/Light2D" are stale tokens (Cross-References, refresh table), not authority.
206	*Edge notes.* `Light2D` appears in this GDD only in the negative or inside a quotation of a stale clause. (orchestrator ruling R2.)
207	
208	**PF-3. Read set and handles.**
209	*Rule.* The Filter reads: `sanity.perception` (local owner only), the SIM view `sanity_view(player_id) -> {stage, tell_on, harm_eligible}`, Graph `true_value(kind, id)` and Suit `true_value(key, player_id)` (it is the **only non-diagnostic caller** of either, LS-19, LS-22, SE-29), the kernel read views of true positions (`horror.view`, Body and Controller views, for placement only), the tick count, `tick_alpha` and the Pipeline's `present_time`. It **holds no handle on `sanity.state` or `sanity.ledger`** ("no Sanity symbol reads a Filter value, and the Filter holds no handle on `sanity.state` or `sanity.ledger`", SN-23). It imports no simulation module, never registers or moves an Interaction subject (IA-13) and never submits a command.
210	*Why.* One wrap point, one place the Debug Overlay hooks, and a one-way edge: Sanity writes, the Filter draws, nothing flows back.
211	*Edge notes.* The HUD never calls Suit's `true_value`; it calls `perceived(SUIT_KEY(k), viewer)`, which wraps it (refresh row 11, X10). The Filter never reads `served_pm`, `lit` or any Attention value to *draw* anything.
212	
213	**PF-4. Default TRUTH, four grades.**
214	*Rule.* Every presentation node under the world layer is TRUTH unless it carries a `PerceptionTag` of another grade. Grades: **TRUTH_PX** (bit-identical pixels with the Filter on or off); **TRUTH_ST** (state, shape, position and existence never moved, added or removed; a colour-only edge tint inside ART 4.4 is allowed); **LEAK** (truth by construction: the leak elements themselves, which "cannot be faked or suppressed by any other lie"); **CORRUPTIBLE** (a named module-body surface carrying a `lie_surface_id` present in `lie_targets.json`). An untagged node is TRUTH (counted in `tag_defaults_applied`, never an error).
215	*Why.* A forgotten node that lies about the consequence channel is the one unrecoverable P1 failure; a forgotten instrument that never lies is a content bug caught by a coverage lint (AC-PF-6). The consequence of default-TRUTH is that the failure mode of omission is "the lie vanishes", never "the truth breaks".

244	| 21 | **Corruptible set, VS-A and VS-B** (designed, tested with stubs) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)*: WORN descriptors (demoted from MVP-live: no `PerceptionRef` exists, PF-9; Sanity's published `surface` set has no WORN value, so it stays VS-A with no ref, OQ-PF-38 item 4 closed 2026-10-28 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*), `suit.*` readings behind `READING_LIE_STAGE`, scanner at stage 3, decoy overlays, phantom rigs, HIDE of a real body, lure dressing, the class-(c) horror rig on a crewmate (beam and voice stay TRUTH) | CORRUPTIBLE | SN-19 to SN-22 |
245	
246	*Why.* P1: "Subtle is allowed; absent is not" applies to the leaks; the closed lists apply to everything else. Rows 17a and 17b follow Sanity's art-director classification over LO-14's "pipe flow" (X5): a running pipe is a world-state witness and its shape is the colour-blind backup. Radiator glow sprite, lamp-housing glow sprite and breaker-panel lamp stay corruptible (LS:213).
247	*Edge notes.* The lamp-housing lie swaps an **appearance frame** only: the real lamp light, pool and `lux` never change (AC-SN-122). **Must repeat (MSA-35, MSA F1):** Assembly reads no `PERCEPTION_OUT` block and writes no perception state; the Filter never wraps seam geometry, bead, cap plate, socket state or `CUT_BLOCKED`, never fakes or suppresses an install prompt, and, until Graph ASK G8 and F&T ASK FT1 are answered, never wraps the sprites of the seam's own PIPE and DUCT valves and CABLE breaker (MSA-23 fallback). MSA-35's allowance of a phantom seam or a false "welded" state in the Filter's corruptible layer is not used: no seam surface is in `lie_targets.json`, and rows 11 and 12 bar one while F1 stands. (orchestrator ruling R11, R13.)
248	
249	**PF-6. Tag contract and lints.**
250	*Rule.* A `PerceptionTag` resource on each presentation scene root carries `{class: TRUTH_PX | TRUTH_ST | LEAK | CORRUPTIBLE, lie_surface_id}`; a CORRUPTIBLE dial or readout surface also carries the calibration record of PF-45 (supplied by the owning scene). The decision logic lives in a headless-testable resolver. Build-failing lints: (i) CORRUPTIBLE requires a `lie_surface_id` present in `lie_targets.json`; (ii) **no TRUTH_PX node has any Filter leak parameter at a non-rest value in any frame**, and on a TRUTH_ST node only `edge_bleed_pm` may be non-rest, and only where the sheet's edge channel is set and its emission channel is clear (PF-24); the lint is at parameter level because the lit leak family lives as a default-off block inside the shared HullSurface and Emissive materials (PF-43), so a node may carry the shared material and still be bit-identical; (iii) the wrapped-sprite registry holds no seam-lane valve or breaker id (row 12); (iv) the Filter source imports no simulation module and writes no block, `Camera2D`, `Viewport`, `SubViewport`, `SubViewportContainer` or real-light member; (v) no Filter code path calls `register_subject`, moves a subject or submits a command (IA-13, AC-IA-85); (vi) coverage: every module kind in `lie_targets.json` has at least one tagged CORRUPTIBLE surface in the MVP content (a VS-A WORN row is not counted and not required, PF-9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; (vii) no Filter code path calls `set_shader_parameter` on a material referenced by more than one node *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
251	*Why.* Behaviour plus lint, not a class layout. -> ADR candidate: tag mechanism and default-deny.
252	*Edge notes.* Lint (ii) is reworded from the rulings' "no Filter material on any TRUTH-tagged node" to parameter level because the stage-3 pipe-edge bleed puts a Filter-written parameter on a shared pipe material whose silhouette edge is graded TRUTH_ST (row 17b) while its emission, chevrons, pattern and diameter stay TRUTH_PX (row 17a); the parameter-level reading keeps the lint testable (CONFLICT C-2 below). (orchestrator ruling R12.)
253	
254	**PF-7. The query.**
255	*Rule.* `perceived(ref: PerceptionRef, viewer: PlayerId) -> Perceived` is the only way a corruptible node obtains a displayed value. It is a pull, called from the render callback, deterministic in `(the sanity.perception entry for ref, the true value, the lie's sim-time age, present_time-driven phases, viewer)` modulo the presentation-local state of PF-11. **Cheap honest path:** with no entry for `ref`, `displayed` equals the true value, `leak_amplitude_pm` is 0, `motion_mode` is HONEST, nothing is allocated. Instruments and the HUD never call `true_value`; the Debug Overlay (DIAGNOSTIC) calls both `true_value` and `perceived` for the same ref (PF-41). Results are memoised per `(ref, viewer, frame)`; an honest ref is further memoised per sanity run and invalidated by the notification that dirtied it (so an honest gauge never lags its own settle).
256	*Why.* One call keeps one wrap point and one debug hook. It mirrors Suit's `true_value(key, player_id)`. The wall gauge, its inspect card and the Debug Overlay's "perceived" column cost one evaluation, and card-gauge parity (HR-14, IA-38) holds by construction.
257	*Edge notes.* Instruments apply their honest settle and tremor **only when `motion_mode` is HONEST**. (orchestrator ruling R8.)
258	
259	**PF-8. The `Perceived` record.**
260	
261	| Field | Type and range | Meaning |
262	|---|---|---|
263	| `displayed_pm` | int 0 to 1000 | the value the needle, readout or glyph shows, as per mille of the instrument's range; wander included; equals the true reading on the honest path |
264	| `displayed_value` | number in the unit of `true_value` for the ref | the same value in the ref's own unit, for numerals and suit keys (derived through the PF-45 calibration); equals `true_value` on the honest path |
265	| `frame_override` | StringName or NONE | the honest state frame to show (SPRITE_SWAP, glow sprite, glyph); NONE on the honest path. For SPRITE_SWAP the frame is `params.frame_id` (Sanity's honest alternate frame); the Filter picks no frame, and PF-19's "one of the machine's own honest state frames" stays true because Sanity's `frame_id` is one *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity's closed schema)* |
266	| `motion_mode` | HONEST, GLIDE, TICK, STALE, BREATH, RETURN | HONEST: Instruments apply settle and tremor. GLIDE: Filter-owned trajectory, no settle. TICK: the readout ticks continuously. STALE: the readout is held. The "readout" is the card numeral (and any digit readout), i.e. the `displayed_value` of the ref's record: TICK and STALE govern that numeral only, and the needle of the same ref draws `displayed_pm`, always with the never-rest wander, in every non-HONEST mode (Instruments C2, OQ-IW-19). BREATH *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a static-pair frame (housing, glyph, machine state) is showing its false state and its gleam breathes between `floor_eff` (D.5) and `AMP_MAX_PM` over 4 to 6 s, the hue-independent mode of that surface class (PF-15 table, D.8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. RETURN: the lie ended and the follower closes the gap; the mode stays RETURN until CLEAR (PF-12, D.5) |
267	| `tick_phase_ms` | int | ms since the last digit change (TICK only) |
268	| `leak_amplitude_pm` | int 0 to 1000 | the gleam amplitude at this instant (PF-15, D.5); gleam only; the sound level is the separate unbreathed `amp_snd` on the audio request *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1/R8)* |
269	| `leak_modes` | bitmask {GLEAM = 1, GLIDE = 2, SOUND = 4} | modes in force after the drop rule; always contains GLEAM and the motion mode (PF-15); bit 2 (named GLIDE, Sanity's "motion bit") stands for the surface class's hue-independent motion mode: needle drift and wander, TICK or STALE, BREATH, or rotor drift *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
270	| `tremor_weight_pm` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | int 0 to 1000 | the share of an honest tremor already in progress that Instruments may still apply: 1000 on the honest path; on a lie's first ACTIVE frame it falls linearly to 0 over `TREMOR_BLEND_S` (:= `WANDER_ONSET_S`) and stays 0 until CLEAR, so a gauge that was trembling at onset blends out instead of stopping dead (the onset rule of PF-17). It never starts a tremor, and a lie never borrows one |
271	| `lie_id` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | int, 0 = none | the lie handle, for logs and the Debug Overlay: Sanity's `lie_id` verbatim (minted per seat at the accept, >= 1, never reused; SN-23) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity publishes `lie_id`)*, so it is non-zero for exactly as long as a lie is ACTIVE or in RETURN and 0 on the honest path. It is kept (with `lie_kind`) through RETURN and becomes 0 (`lie_kind` NONE) only at CLEAR (S3 `NONE`) (OQ-DO-2 (v)). The Debug Overlay's `lie_id != 0` discriminator (DO-21) and its join by (viewer, subject_ref) are unchanged |
272	| `lie_kind` | FALSE_OK, FALSE_FAIL, GLIDE, SPRITE_SWAP, NONE | echo of Sanity's kind |
273	
274	*Rule.* The record **never contains the true value** when a lie is active; it is what the seat *perceives*. A remote `viewer` returns the honest record (PF-10). *Why.* A record that carried the truth beside the lie would hand the HUD a way to leak it. The record is a request to Instruments and the HUD, not their design.
275	
276	**PF-9. `PerceptionRef`.**
277	*Rule.* The ref is a tagged union: `GRAPH_NODE(kind, id)`, `GRAPH_COMPARTMENT(cid, quantity)` (the `quantity` term, one of the Instruments IW-9 quantities, keeps two compartment instruments in one room distinct in the PF-7 memo and selects the `true_value` kind; K-5, OQ-IW-26), `SUIT_KEY(key)` (the five keys `suit.o2`, `suit.reserve`, `suit.integrity`, `suit.warmth`, `suit.charge`), `SCANNER`, `HOUSING_GLOW(ref)`, `STATE_GLYPH(ref)`, `MACHINE_FRAME(ref)`. The inspect card uses the **same ref** as the wall gauge it mirrors: there is no separate card ref and no separate lie. A ref resolves to Sanity's `subject_ref` through the tag's `lie_surface_id` plus the Graph id *(provisional — the Graph-node-to-subject mapping is the one named assumption of SN-16's lit-entry rule, routed to Interaction and Derelict Authoring)*. A stable integer `ref_key` (kind, id and, for a compartment, `quantity`; never an instance id) feeds the hash (PF-37).
278	*Why.* One union, one wrap point (orchestrator ruling D11). Suit rail counts are not keys (SE OQ-6) and stay anchors.
279	**The join: Sanity's `subject_ref` to a `PerceptionRef`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity's closed schema)*. Each row of the Sanity-owned `lie_targets.json` is a pair (module kind, surface kind) and each ledger `subject_ref` is the published pair `{stable_id: String, surface: int}` (surface 1 NEEDLE, 2 READOUT, 3 GLYPH, 4 GLOW_SPRITE, 5 MACHINE_SPRITE; SN-23). `quantity` is NOT part of the key: a compartment gauge is its own instrument with its own `stable_id` (IW-8 `instrument_id`), so two gauges in one room are two keys; the `quantity`, node id or `cid` are read by the constructor from the instrument record found by `stable_id` (`lie_targets.json` row plus IW-8 record) and feed the `PerceptionRef` and `ref_key`, never the join. The Filter resolves it with exactly one constructor, so a lie can never attach to two refs and a ref can never receive two lies from one entry (AC-PF-112 tests the bijection on every row).
280	
281	| Sanity `surface` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity's closed schema)* | IW-8 facet of `lie_surface_id` | `PerceptionRef` built from the record | True source (read only by the Filter) |
282	|---|---|---|---|
283	| 1 NEEDLE | `<instrument_id>.needle` | `GRAPH_NODE(kind, id)` or `GRAPH_COMPARTMENT(cid, quantity)` per the record's `node_ref` / `room_key` / `quantity` (wall gauge and card share this ref, HR-14) | Graph `true_value` |
284	| 2 READOUT | `.needle` of a `gauge_kind` READOUT instrument | same constructor | Graph `true_value` |
285	| 3 GLYPH | `.glyph` | `STATE_GLYPH(GRAPH_NODE)` | the node's state |
286	| 4 GLOW_SPRITE | `.housing_glow` | `HOUSING_GLOW(GRAPH_NODE of the lamp)` | appearance frame only (the light and `lux` stay TRUTH) |
287	| 5 MACHINE_SPRITE | `.machine_frame` | `MACHINE_FRAME(GRAPH_NODE)` | the node's state, both honest frames required |
288	
289	`SUIT_KEY`, `SCANNER` and WORN have no `surface` value at MVP (honest paths; Sanity lists none; WORN stays VS-A with no ref type, PF-5 row 21, out of the MVP coverage lint, PF-6 vi; `SCANNER` has no published true source, OQ-PF-36). A listed `surface` outside 1 to 5, or one that does not match the record's `gauge_kind`, draws nothing and counts `lie_unrenderable`. The inspect card is not a surface (it is drawn from the NEEDLE or READOUT ref, HR-14), matching Sanity. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*
290	
291	**PF-10. Per-viewer scope.**
292	*Rule.* The Filter answers for the **local seat only**. A remote PlayerId passed to `perceived` returns the honest record (counter `remote_queries`); it is never an error. Addressing is by PlayerId, never `peer_id`. `sanity.perception` is `OWNER_PRIVATE`; the replicated `SHARED_SUMMARY` `{stage, tell_on, harm_eligible}` is what lets viewer A draw seat B's tell fringe (VS-B).
293	*Why.* Answering a remote PlayerId from replicated data would let a client compute another's lies (SN-26). (orchestrator ruling R9.)
294	
295	#### B. The lie: clock, trajectory, leak, end
296	
297	**PF-11. Lie clock and purity.**
298	*Rule.* A lie's trajectory runs on **sim time**, clocked from the lie's **activation run**: `lie_tau = (T_c - SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR * act_run + tick_alpha) / TICK_RATE`, with `SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR` 12 (registered; equal to the kernel hook divisor by relation, not a knob), `TICK_RATE` 60, `act_run` the run on which the entry became ACTIVE, clamped at 0 (D.1). Pause freezes the tick and therefore the lie. Presentation phases that carry no information (wander phase, breath phase, tick cadence) run on `present_time` (PIPE PR-9). The displayed value is a **pure function of the entry, the live true value, `lie_tau` and per-lie constants, modulo PRESENTATION-local state**: the single slew state of PF-13 and PF-14, which is never persisted and is rebuilt from the formula on `hard_start` (PF-33). While a lie is ACTIVE its displayed value is the formula's value, so a restore reproduces it **up to the slew gap that was still closing at the save** (D.3, PF-33) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the per-lie constants (rate, magnitude, wander frequency and phase, tick stagger and sign, sound-breath period) are restore-exact because their hash key is the saved `lie_id` (in the saved ledger, with its counter `next_lie_id`), and `epoch` is 0 for every per-lie draw (D.14); the GLIDE direction and the numeral mode are not hash draws but published entry fields (`direction`, `params.readout_mode`; PF-13, PF-18), saved with the entry *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity publishes `lie_id`, `direction`, `readout_mode`)*. `start_run` and `active_run` are used for the clock only.
299	*Why.* A trajectory on `present_time` would restart from phase 0 after a restore and show a different displayed value (breaking PF-33); a trajectory on sim time is restore-exact and pause-consistent. A lie is a moving value of the world, so it is interpolated with `tick_alpha` (PIPE PR-8 rule 5), not an animation (rule 6): the world moved, so the lie must have advanced. The clock starts at **activation**, not at the accept: Sanity stamps `start_run` at the accept (SN-16, EC-SN-29) and activates `ONSET_DELAY_RUNS` (10 to 25 runs, 2 to 5 s) later, so a clock from `start_run` would put the first ACTIVE frame 2 to 5 s into the glide, a first-frame jump of up to 10 deg that PF-13 and SNV-13 forbid.
300	Sanity publishes `active_run` in the perception entry (registry `sanity.perception`); `act_run` is that field.
301	*Edge notes.* This is the wording the systems-designer proposed for the "pure function" ruling (C-SD2): the lie never snaps (SNV-11), so a step in the true value needs a slew state, and R8's purity holds up to that state. (orchestrator ruling: R8 amended in the live text.)
302	
303	**PF-12. Lie presentation lifecycle** (Sanity's PENDING, ACTIVE, EXPIRED, DEBUNKED, INVALIDATED mapped to pixels).
304	
305	| Sanity state | Filter presentation | Notes |
306	|---|---|---|
307	| PENDING | nothing drawn; `perceived` honest | invisible by SN-16; no pre-onset hint |
308	| ACTIVE, onset | ONSET: the displayed value departs the true value on the glide path from displayed-minus-true = 0; the gleam is already at `floor_eff` (D.5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; the sound request is already on | no first-frame jump; the leak is born with the lie |
309	| ACTIVE, arrived | HOLD: the displayed value sits at its false region with wander (PF-17); the leak is steady | never rests |
310	| EXPIRED, DEBUNKED or INVALIDATED (the entry has left `sanity.perception`) | RETURN: a rate-limited follower closes the gap to the live true value at `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE`; the leak follows the remaining discrepancy through a downward-rate-limited follower (D.5); `lie_id`, `lie_kind` and `leak_modes` stay as they were until CLEAR *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the sound level follows the leak, then off at CLEAR | **presentation-identical for all three end types**; no verdict flash, no relief cue |
311	| **CLEAR** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* = the *later* of three conditions: displayed-minus-true discrepancy under `LEAK_EPS_DEG` (`[PLACEHOLDER]` 0.25 deg; range 0.1 to 0.5; registered); gleam amplitude at 0 (D.5); wander faded to 0 (`WANDER_BLEND_S` after removal, D.6) | CLEAR: `motion_mode` returns to HONEST without an event, `lie_id` and `lie_kind` become 0 and NONE on that frame, the sound request goes OFF; honest settle is allowed again | the mode returns without a signal; until CLEAR the record is a RETURN record, so a gleam is never reported on an honest record and a wander is never faded under an honest label |

### Core Rules

*Conventions.* Rules are named `PF-n`; each states a **Rule**, a **Why** and **Edge notes**. Formulas are `D.n` (Formulas section, written in part 2 of this document; the rules below fix *what* each formula must compute and its binding constants, and name it). Every pixel measure is in **art px of the 640x360 base picture**; on screen it is `k` times larger at integer zoom `k` in `[1, k_auto + 2]` (`k_auto = floor(min(W/640, H/360))`, PIPE PR-1, C6). Registry constants are cited by **name and registry value**; a number marked `[PLACEHOLDER]` is invented here, carries a range and a proposed registered name, and is final nowhere (reflexion: a placeholder never becomes a fact). Upstream facts are cited by rule id first (`SN-15 L-L`, `HE-40`). Anything about Accessibility Settings or Co-op Session is **(provisional — undesigned)**; HUD & Suit Layer, In-World Instruments & Inspect View, Debug Overlay (True Values) and Adaptive Audio & Tells have since been designed and their answers are recorded in Interactions I-B and OQ-PF-29 (2026-10-27 consistency pass). For the undesigned neighbours: this GDD places a requirement on the neighbour and describes what the Filter *returns*, never the neighbour's internals. There is no `scripting.md` or `core.md` in `docs/engine-reference/godot/`: GDScript integer-overflow, `Dictionary` ordering, `RefCounted` lifetime and per-call cost are **not sourceable** and are marked `[UNV]` wherever a rule depends on them; the reference also carries nothing on `canvas_item` shader instance parameters, container materials or viewport masking, so every shading-language mechanism is a `[UNV]` spike item, never the basis of a rule.

#### A. Architecture, channels and the tag contract

**PF-1. Channel architecture: consume, do not own.**
*Rule.* The Filter registers no kernel block, no step hook and no mutator (KERN CR-3, CR-8, CR-9). The `PERCEPTION_OUT` block of the routed thread is `sanity.perception`, which the Filter consumes. The Filter's **perceived channel** (the `Perceived` records, the lie trajectories, the per-viewer decoy list, the rim and outline state) is a presentation-side surface that inherits every `PERCEPTION_OUT` rule: no simulation system reads it (kernel H5), it is never persisted, it is never part of `state_hash` (KERN D.12). KERN C.3 row 11 grants the Filter "Subscriptions only ... Neither gets submit or mutators"; it subscribes as `PRESENTATION`.
*Why.* A `PRESENTATION` subscriber cannot write a block (H3, H4), and the kernel defines the class as Sanity's output. Stating the reading on page one keeps a reviewer from reading the thread literally.
*Edge notes.* Lighting's row says "a per-client `PERCEPTION_OUT` decoy list"; under this rule that list is a Filter-published presentation list (refresh row 20). -> ADR candidate: Filter channel architecture and the "no block" ruling. (orchestrator ruling R1.)

**PF-2. Write set.**
*Rule.* The Filter writes `CanvasItem` members, `Material` and shader parameters (including per-instance parameters), particle members and audio *requests*. It writes **no member of any real light** (LO-25 (ii): "the Filter writes no `Light2D` member"), no `Camera2D`, `Viewport`, `SubViewport` or `SubViewportContainer` property (PIPE C1, C9; the container's `material` slot is assigned and nulled by the pipeline root, PF-25), no simulation state and no block. A grep-able lint enforces every clause (AC-PF-8).
*Why.* The true reveal radius is an anchor (EM-29); a Filter-written light member would be a path to move it. The six upstream clauses that still say "CanvasItem/Material/Light2D" are stale tokens (Cross-References, refresh table), not authority.
*Edge notes.* `Light2D` appears in this GDD only in the negative or inside a quotation of a stale clause. (orchestrator ruling R2.)

**PF-3. Read set and handles.**
*Rule.* The Filter reads: `sanity.perception` (local owner only), the SIM view `sanity_view(player_id) -> {stage, tell_on, harm_eligible}`, Graph `true_value(kind, id)` and Suit `true_value(key, player_id)` (it is the **only non-diagnostic caller** of either, LS-19, LS-22, SE-29), the kernel read views of true positions (`horror.view`, Body and Controller views, for placement only), the tick count, `tick_alpha` and the Pipeline's `present_time`. It **holds no handle on `sanity.state` or `sanity.ledger`** ("no Sanity symbol reads a Filter value, and the Filter holds no handle on `sanity.state` or `sanity.ledger`", SN-23). It imports no simulation module, never registers or moves an Interaction subject (IA-13) and never submits a command.
*Why.* One wrap point, one place the Debug Overlay hooks, and a one-way edge: Sanity writes, the Filter draws, nothing flows back.
*Edge notes.* The HUD never calls Suit's `true_value`; it calls `perceived(SUIT_KEY(k), viewer)`, which wraps it (refresh row 11, X10). The Filter never reads `served_pm`, `lit` or any Attention value to *draw* anything.

**PF-4. Default TRUTH, four grades.**
*Rule.* Every presentation node under the world layer is TRUTH unless it carries a `PerceptionTag` of another grade. Grades: **TRUTH_PX** (bit-identical pixels with the Filter on or off); **TRUTH_ST** (state, shape, position and existence never moved, added or removed; a colour-only edge tint inside ART 4.4 is allowed); **LEAK** (truth by construction: the leak elements themselves, which "cannot be faked or suppressed by any other lie"); **CORRUPTIBLE** (a named module-body surface carrying a `lie_surface_id` present in `lie_targets.json`). An untagged node is TRUTH (counted in `tag_defaults_applied`, never an error).
*Why.* A forgotten node that lies about the consequence channel is the one unrecoverable P1 failure; a forgotten instrument that never lies is a content bug caught by a coverage lint (AC-PF-6). The consequence of default-TRUTH is that the failure mode of omission is "the lie vanishes", never "the truth breaks".
*Edge notes.* Layout's request that walls be truth is granted in full at grade TRUTH_ST (colour-only tint allowed, geometry never touched); Layout's narrower fallback (ordinary interior door leaves at the Filter's discretion) is recorded, not adopted (OQ-PF-14). (orchestrator ruling R11.)

**PF-5. The truth-channel union (table of record)** (registry: `truth_channel_union`).
*Rule.* The **CONSEQUENCE CHANNEL** is the closed list of LS-14: trail VFX (mist, drip, frost, scorch, debris, puddle), the `acoustic` classes at a descriptor's anchor, Suit body cues, lamp brightness from `served_pm`, the `AIRFLOW` draught and the `SEAL_STRAIN` strain; "Perception may neither remove, alter nor add". No lie adds scorch, mist, drip, frost, puddle, sparks or a hiss. The **module-body channel** (a module's sprite, gauge and inspect card, with WORN descriptors from VS-A, LS:864 and LS-14) is the corruptible set *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)*. The union below is assembled once from every neighbour's ask; each row names its grade and the rule that owns the item.

| # | Item | Grade | Owner rule (source) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Trail VFX (mist, drip, frost, scorch, debris, puddle, hairlines) and the stamps' emissive layers; the mask is per trail element, not per layer (a pipe edge may bleed beside a frost fan; the fan never) | TRUTH_PX | LS-14; FT-2; FT AC-4, AC-5; FT E22 |
| 2 | The `acoustic` classes at descriptor anchors (HISS, DRIP, HUM_DROP, CLANK, WIND, TICK, SIZZLE, CREAK); relay clunk; cavitation TICK | TRUTH (audio) | LS-14; SN-25 |
| 3 | Suit body cues (breath step, visor fog, rime, shiver, reserve valve click, load layer, seam jet, HEAVY back-frame, stagger, walk-only); the 5.3 vital overlays; the warning mark; rail counts (anchors) | TRUTH_PX | SE-25, SE-27, SE-29; SN-19 |
| 4 | Lamp brightness from `served_pm`; the floor light pool; `lux`; fault-glow light; every real light's reach, edge, colour and shadow; the beam, local and remote; the **true reveal radius** | TRUTH_PX | EM-29; LO-25, LO-28; `modifier_stack` |
| 5 | `AIRFLOW` draught; `SEAL_STRAIN` creak and strain | TRUTH | LS-14 |
| 6 | Attention outputs: `web_strand_*`, `vfx_tell_*`, band slide, filaments, tell audio, dust-direction change | TRUTH_PX; exclusive to Attention's presenter; **"its anchor list includes the tell cues"** | AT-17; AT AV-17, AV-18; AC-AT-41, AC-AT-113; AT E-55 |

MSA-35's allowance of a phantom seam or a false "welded" state in the Filter's corruptible layer is not used: no seam surface is in `lie_targets.json`, and rows 11 and 12 bar one while F1 stands. (orchestrator ruling R11, R13.)

**PF-6. Tag contract and lints.**
*Rule.* A `PerceptionTag` resource on each presentation scene root carries `{class: TRUTH_PX | TRUTH_ST | LEAK | CORRUPTIBLE, lie_surface_id}`; a CORRUPTIBLE dial or readout surface also carries the calibration record of PF-45 (supplied by the owning scene). The decision logic lives in a headless-testable resolver. Build-failing lints: (i) CORRUPTIBLE requires a `lie_surface_id` present in `lie_targets.json`; (ii) **no TRUTH_PX node has any Filter leak parameter at a non-rest value in any frame**, and on a TRUTH_ST node only `edge_bleed_pm` may be non-rest, and only where the sheet's edge channel is set and its emission channel is clear (PF-24); the lint is at parameter level because the lit leak family lives as a default-off block inside the shared HullSurface and Emissive materials (PF-43), so a node may carry the shared material and still be bit-identical; (iii) the wrapped-sprite registry holds no seam-lane valve or breaker id (row 12); (iv) the Filter source imports no simulation module and writes no block, `Camera2D`, `Viewport`, `SubViewport`, `SubViewportContainer` or real-light member; (v) no Filter code path calls `register_subject`, moves a subject or submits a command (IA-13, AC-IA-85); (vi) coverage: every module kind in `lie_targets.json` has at least one tagged CORRUPTIBLE surface in the MVP content (a VS-A WORN row is not counted and not required, PF-9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; (vii) no Filter code path calls `set_shader_parameter` on a material referenced by more than one node *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
*Why.* Behaviour plus lint, not a class layout. -> ADR candidate: tag mechanism and default-deny.
*Edge notes.* Lint (ii) is reworded from the rulings' "no Filter material on any TRUTH-tagged node" to parameter level because the stage-3 pipe-edge bleed puts a Filter-written parameter on a shared pipe material whose silhouette edge is graded TRUTH_ST (row 17b) while its emission, chevrons, pattern and diameter stay TRUTH_PX (row 17a); the parameter-level reading keeps the lint testable (CONFLICT C-2 below). (orchestrator ruling R12.)

**PF-7. The query.**
*Rule.* `perceived(ref: PerceptionRef, viewer: PlayerId) -> Perceived` is the only way a corruptible node obtains a displayed value. It is a pull, called from the render callback, deterministic in `(the sanity.perception entry for ref, the true value, the lie's sim-time age, present_time-driven phases, viewer)` modulo the presentation-local state of PF-11. **Cheap honest path:** with no entry for `ref`, `displayed` equals the true value, `leak_amplitude_pm` is 0, `motion_mode` is HONEST, nothing is allocated. Instruments and the HUD never call `true_value`; the Debug Overlay (DIAGNOSTIC) calls both `true_value` and `perceived` for the same ref (PF-41). Results are memoised per `(ref, viewer, frame)`; an honest ref is further memoised per sanity run and invalidated by the notification that dirtied it (so an honest gauge never lags its own settle).
*Why.* One call keeps one wrap point and one debug hook. It mirrors Suit's `true_value(key, player_id)`. The wall gauge, its inspect card and the Debug Overlay's "perceived" column cost one evaluation, and card-gauge parity (HR-14, IA-38) holds by construction.
*Edge notes.* Instruments apply their honest settle and tremor **only when `motion_mode` is HONEST**. (orchestrator ruling R8.)

**PF-8. The `Perceived` record.**

| Field | Type and range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `displayed_pm` | int 0 to 1000 | the value the needle, readout or glyph shows, as per mille of the instrument's range; wander included; equals the true reading on the honest path |
| `displayed_value` | number in the unit of `true_value` for the ref | the same value in the ref's own unit, for numerals and suit keys (derived through the PF-45 calibration); equals `true_value` on the honest path |
| `frame_override` | StringName or NONE | the honest state frame to show (SPRITE_SWAP, glow sprite, glyph); NONE on the honest path. For SPRITE_SWAP the frame is `params.frame_id` (Sanity's honest alternate frame); the Filter picks no frame, and PF-19's "one of the machine's own honest state frames" stays true because Sanity's `frame_id` is one *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity's closed schema)* |
| `motion_mode` | HONEST, GLIDE, TICK, STALE, BREATH, RETURN | HONEST: Instruments apply settle and tremor. GLIDE: Filter-owned trajectory, no settle. TICK: the readout ticks continuously. STALE: the readout is held. The "readout" is the card numeral (and any digit readout), i.e. the `displayed_value` of the ref's record: TICK and STALE govern that numeral only, and the needle of the same ref draws `displayed_pm`, always with the never-rest wander, in every non-HONEST mode (Instruments C2, OQ-IW-19). BREATH *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a static-pair frame (housing, glyph, machine state) is showing its false state and its gleam breathes between `floor_eff` (D.5) and `AMP_MAX_PM` over 4 to 6 s, the hue-independent mode of that surface class (PF-15 table, D.8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. RETURN: the lie ended and the follower closes the gap; the mode stays RETURN until CLEAR (PF-12, D.5) |
| `tick_phase_ms` | int | ms since the last digit change (TICK only) |
| `leak_amplitude_pm` | int 0 to 1000 | the gleam amplitude at this instant (PF-15, D.5); gleam only; the sound level is the separate unbreathed `amp_snd` on the audio request *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1/R8)* |
| `leak_modes` | bitmask {GLEAM = 1, GLIDE = 2, SOUND = 4} | modes in force after the drop rule; always contains GLEAM and the motion mode (PF-15); bit 2 (named GLIDE, Sanity's "motion bit") stands for the surface class's hue-independent motion mode: needle drift and wander, TICK or STALE, BREATH, or rotor drift *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `tremor_weight_pm` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | int 0 to 1000 | the share of an honest tremor already in progress that Instruments may still apply: 1000 on the honest path; on a lie's first ACTIVE frame it falls linearly to 0 over `TREMOR_BLEND_S` (:= `WANDER_ONSET_S`) and stays 0 until CLEAR, so a gauge that was trembling at onset blends out instead of stopping dead (the onset rule of PF-17). It never starts a tremor, and a lie never borrows one |
| `lie_id` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | int, 0 = none | the lie handle, for logs and the Debug Overlay: Sanity's `lie_id` verbatim (minted per seat at the accept, >= 1, never reused; SN-23) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity publishes `lie_id`)*, so it is non-zero for exactly as long as a lie is ACTIVE or in RETURN and 0 on the honest path. It is kept (with `lie_kind`) through RETURN and becomes 0 (`lie_kind` NONE) only at CLEAR (S3 `NONE`) (OQ-DO-2 (v)). The Debug Overlay's `lie_id != 0` discriminator (DO-21) and its join by (viewer, subject_ref) are unchanged |
| `lie_kind` | FALSE_OK, FALSE_FAIL, GLIDE, SPRITE_SWAP, NONE | echo of Sanity's kind |

*Rule.* The record **never contains the true value** when a lie is active; it is what the seat *perceives*. A remote `viewer` returns the honest record (PF-10). *Why.* A record that carried the truth beside the lie would hand the HUD a way to leak it. The record is a request to Instruments and the HUD, not their design.

**PF-9. `PerceptionRef`.**
*Rule.* The ref is a tagged union: `GRAPH_NODE(kind, id)`, `GRAPH_COMPARTMENT(cid, quantity)` (the `quantity` term, one of the Instruments IW-9 quantities, keeps two compartment instruments in one room distinct in the PF-7 memo and selects the `true_value` kind; K-5, OQ-IW-26), `SUIT_KEY(key)` (the five keys `suit.o2`, `suit.reserve`, `suit.integrity`, `suit.warmth`, `suit.charge`), `SCANNER`, `HOUSING_GLOW(ref)`, `STATE_GLYPH(ref)`, `MACHINE_FRAME(ref)`. The inspect card uses the **same ref** as the wall gauge it mirrors: there is no separate card ref and no separate lie. A ref resolves to Sanity's `subject_ref` through the tag's `lie_surface_id` plus the Graph id *(provisional — the Graph-node-to-subject mapping is the one named assumption of SN-16's lit-entry rule, routed to Interaction and Derelict Authoring)*. A stable integer `ref_key` (kind, id and, for a compartment, `quantity`; never an instance id) feeds the hash (PF-37).
*Why.* One union, one wrap point (orchestrator ruling D11). Suit rail counts are not keys (SE OQ-6) and stay anchors.
**The join: Sanity's `subject_ref` to a `PerceptionRef`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity's closed schema)*. Each row of the Sanity-owned `lie_targets.json` is a pair (module kind, surface kind) and each ledger `subject_ref` is the published pair `{stable_id: String, surface: int}` (surface 1 NEEDLE, 2 READOUT, 3 GLYPH, 4 GLOW_SPRITE, 5 MACHINE_SPRITE; SN-23). `quantity` is NOT part of the key: a compartment gauge is its own instrument with its own `stable_id` (IW-8 `instrument_id`), so two gauges in one room are two keys; the `quantity`, node id or `cid` are read by the constructor from the instrument record found by `stable_id` (`lie_targets.json` row plus IW-8 record) and feed the `PerceptionRef` and `ref_key`, never the join. The Filter resolves it with exactly one constructor, so a lie can never attach to two refs and a ref can never receive two lies from one entry (AC-PF-112 tests the bijection on every row).

| Sanity `surface` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity's closed schema)* | IW-8 facet of `lie_surface_id` | `PerceptionRef` built from the record | True source (read only by the Filter) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 NEEDLE | `<instrument_id>.needle` | `GRAPH_NODE(kind, id)` or `GRAPH_COMPARTMENT(cid, quantity)` per the record's `node_ref` / `room_key` / `quantity` (wall gauge and card share this ref, HR-14) | Graph `true_value` |
| 2 READOUT | `.needle` of a `gauge_kind` READOUT instrument | same constructor | Graph `true_value` |
| 3 GLYPH | `.glyph` | `STATE_GLYPH(GRAPH_NODE)` | the node's state |
| 4 GLOW_SPRITE | `.housing_glow` | `HOUSING_GLOW(GRAPH_NODE of the lamp)` | appearance frame only (the light and `lux` stay TRUTH) |
| 5 MACHINE_SPRITE | `.machine_frame` | `MACHINE_FRAME(GRAPH_NODE)` | the node's state, both honest frames required |

`SUIT_KEY`, `SCANNER` and WORN have no `surface` value at MVP (honest paths; Sanity lists none; WORN stays VS-A with no ref type, PF-5 row 21, out of the MVP coverage lint, PF-6 vi; `SCANNER` has no published true source, OQ-PF-36). A listed `surface` outside 1 to 5, or one that does not match the record's `gauge_kind`, draws nothing and counts `lie_unrenderable`. The inspect card is not a surface (it is drawn from the NEEDLE or READOUT ref, HR-14), matching Sanity. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*

**PF-10. Per-viewer scope.**
*Rule.* The Filter answers for the **local seat only**. A remote PlayerId passed to `perceived` returns the honest record (counter `remote_queries`); it is never an error. Addressing is by PlayerId, never `peer_id`. `sanity.perception` is `OWNER_PRIVATE`; the replicated `SHARED_SUMMARY` `{stage, tell_on, harm_eligible}` is what lets viewer A draw seat B's tell fringe (VS-B).
*Why.* Answering a remote PlayerId from replicated data would let a client compute another's lies (SN-26). (orchestrator ruling R9.)

#### B. The lie: clock, trajectory, leak, end

**PF-11. Lie clock and purity.**
*Rule.* A lie's trajectory runs on **sim time**, clocked from the lie's **activation run**: `lie_tau = (T_c - SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR * act_run + tick_alpha) / TICK_RATE`, with `SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR` 12 (registered; equal to the kernel hook divisor by relation, not a knob), `TICK_RATE` 60, `act_run` the run on which the entry became ACTIVE, clamped at 0 (D.1). Pause freezes the tick and therefore the lie. Presentation phases that carry no information (wander phase, breath phase, tick cadence) run on `present_time` (PIPE PR-9). The displayed value is a **pure function of the entry, the live true value, `lie_tau` and per-lie constants, modulo PRESENTATION-local state**: the single slew state of PF-13 and PF-14, which is never persisted and is rebuilt from the formula on `hard_start` (PF-33). While a lie is ACTIVE its displayed value is the formula's value, so a restore reproduces it **up to the slew gap that was still closing at the save** (D.3, PF-33) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the per-lie constants (rate, magnitude, wander frequency and phase, tick stagger and sign, sound-breath period) are restore-exact because their hash key is the saved `lie_id` (in the saved ledger, with its counter `next_lie_id`), and `epoch` is 0 for every per-lie draw (D.14); the GLIDE direction and the numeral mode are not hash draws but published entry fields (`direction`, `params.readout_mode`; PF-13, PF-18), saved with the entry *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity publishes `lie_id`, `direction`, `readout_mode`)*. `start_run` and `active_run` are used for the clock only.
*Why.* A trajectory on `present_time` would restart from phase 0 after a restore and show a different displayed value (breaking PF-33); a trajectory on sim time is restore-exact and pause-consistent. A lie is a moving value of the world, so it is interpolated with `tick_alpha` (PIPE PR-8 rule 5), not an animation (rule 6): the world moved, so the lie must have advanced. The clock starts at **activation**, not at the accept: Sanity stamps `start_run` at the accept (SN-16, EC-SN-29) and activates `ONSET_DELAY_RUNS` (10 to 25 runs, 2 to 5 s) later, so a clock from `start_run` would put the first ACTIVE frame 2 to 5 s into the glide, a first-frame jump of up to 10 deg that PF-13 and SNV-13 forbid.
Sanity publishes `active_run` in the perception entry (registry `sanity.perception`); `act_run` is that field.
*Edge notes.* This is the wording the systems-designer proposed for the "pure function" ruling (C-SD2): the lie never snaps (SNV-11), so a step in the true value needs a slew state, and R8's purity holds up to that state. (orchestrator ruling: R8 amended in the live text.)

**PF-12. Lie presentation lifecycle** (Sanity's PENDING, ACTIVE, EXPIRED, DEBUNKED, INVALIDATED mapped to pixels).

| Sanity state | Filter presentation | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| PENDING | nothing drawn; `perceived` honest | invisible by SN-16; no pre-onset hint |
| ACTIVE, onset | ONSET: the displayed value departs the true value on the glide path from displayed-minus-true = 0; the gleam is already at `floor_eff` (D.5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; the sound request is already on | no first-frame jump; the leak is born with the lie |
| ACTIVE, arrived | HOLD: the displayed value sits at its false region with wander (PF-17); the leak is steady | never rests |
| EXPIRED, DEBUNKED or INVALIDATED (the entry has left `sanity.perception`) | RETURN: a rate-limited follower closes the gap to the live true value at `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE`; the leak follows the remaining discrepancy through a downward-rate-limited follower (D.5); `lie_id`, `lie_kind` and `leak_modes` stay as they were until CLEAR *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the sound level follows the leak, then off at CLEAR | **presentation-identical for all three end types**; no verdict flash, no relief cue |
| **CLEAR** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* = the *later* of three conditions: displayed-minus-true discrepancy under `LEAK_EPS_DEG` (`[PLACEHOLDER]` 0.25 deg; range 0.1 to 0.5; registered); gleam amplitude at 0 (D.5); wander faded to 0 (`WANDER_BLEND_S` after removal, D.6) | CLEAR: `motion_mode` returns to HONEST without an event, `lie_id` and `lie_kind` become 0 and NONE on that frame, the sound request goes OFF; honest settle is allowed again | the mode returns without a signal; until CLEAR the record is a RETURN record, so a gleam is never reported on an honest record and a wander is never faded under an honest label |

435	#### E. Geometry, safety, ordering and budget
436	
437	**PF-31. Leak geometry at every ladder step and both passes.**
438	*Rule.* All fringes, gleams and bands are defined in **art px** and drawn inside the world render at world resolution, never as a post-process on the upscaled container: `n` art px is `n * k` screen px at ladder step `k` (D.10), and the width is always an exact integer multiple of `k` (no sub-art-pixel softness) at **every** `k in [1, k_auto + 2]` (1 to 5 at 1080p, 1 to 8 at 2160p), under render pass A and pass B (pass B takes `k` as a uniform, PIPE:182). Geometry is sampled in texels of the sprite's own texture where possible, so it is pass-agnostic for free; the rim band is sourced from Lighting's four beam-edge mask sprites. A zoom change is a cut (PIPE C6): leak widths are re-derived on the first frame of the new rung and never interpolated across `k`. The drawn marks are sprites or quads, never `draw_line` (4.7 lines lose their antialias feather); no mark is narrower than 1 art px; nearest sampling only; luminance at or below 0.9 x `GLOW_HDR_THRESHOLD`.
439	*Why.* SNV-29; reflexion: an invariant written against "the default" zoom must be re-checked at every reachable rung. At `k` 1 on 2160p a 2 px band is 2 screen px on a 3840x2160 field: legibility at the Deck is an Open Question (PIPE OQ 4, OQ-PF-4).
440	*Edge notes.* Character and horror cells keep at least 2 transparent px outside the contour for the outline (target 4 px; the 2-versus-4 reconciliation is the art-director's, 8.2). An outline never covers a sprite pixel (`show_behind_parent`-class).
441	
442	**PF-32. Flash and photosensitivity: the bound pair.**
443	*Rule.* The Filter's luminance ramps (gleam, fringe breath, hue bleed, stage envelopes) are not Lighting-originated and do not enter LO-22's governor; the Filter **self-governs by construction**. The binding bound is always the **pair**: PIPE PR-13 (at most `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3 flashes per rolling 1 s, per light, per region of **a ninth of the displayed picture at the current field**, and on the frame mean; a flash is a pair of opposing luminance changes of at least 10 %, red included) **and** HR-13 (no HUD element changes luminance faster than 3 Hz). No full-frame flash on any layer. Every Filter source is amplitude-continuous, **except the rise-only onset step** (0 to `floor_eff` on the first ACTIVE frame, SNV-13: a single-direction change on one gleam element, followed by no fall for at least half a breath period because a lie's gleam breath starts at its trough, D.8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and its modelled opposing-pair magnitude inside any rolling second stays under 10 % at the patch level and far under it at the region level (D.11; the ramps are monotone, the breath is a raised cosine whose turning points are at least 2 s apart), and the verification is a 60 s flash scan at stage 3 at the **largest field** (zoom 1x on 2160p, 36 times the 640x360 area).
444	*Why.* "Region = a ninth of the displayed picture at the current field" (LO-22) supersedes PIPE D.15's "213x120 fixed" (refresh row 10, X11).
445	*Edge notes.* Reduce-flashing is a separate toggle from reduced motion; Filter ramps are already flash-free, so it changes nothing here (PF-39).
446	
447	**PF-33. No clean frame.**
448	*Rule.* The first RUNNING frame after LOADING, and the first frame after any `force_stage` or `force_level`, is presented **already filtered**: envelopes are set to their targets (`hard_start`), lies are drawn at the formula's value for the restored `lie_tau` with full leak from frame one, and `perceived` is answerable before the first RUNNING frame (Sanity rebuilds `sanity.perception` in `post_restore`, SN-23). No fade-in from clean. Glide and breath *phase* and the slew state may differ after restore; **while a lie is ACTIVE** its presence, kind, leak and displayed value (by PF-11) do not: the first frame shows the formula's value, which equals the pre-save value except for any slew gap that was still closing at the save (D.3), and a return in progress at the save is not restored (the entry had already left `sanity.perception`; E-PF-5). Counter `first_frame_filtered`.
449	*Why.* "One unfiltered frame would be a free oracle" (SN-23); AC-SL-124: "the first `RUNNING` frame after `LOADING` must already be presented through the Perception Filter for the restored sanity level - the black hold covers any rebuild". This answers SL OQ-11 as co-owner with Sanity and the Pipeline. (orchestrator ruling R20.)
450	
451	**PF-34. Unseen lies and no leak culling.**
452	*Rule.* A listed lie is drawn whenever its surface is on screen and lit; there is no "seat away" special case; its trajectory is a function of sim time and reappears at the correct point. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6 GAP; Sanity now lists away entries, SN-23 `away`)* Sanity keeps an entry listed while the seat is in another compartment (`away` true), so a lie seen through an open door, from a hatch or at a zoomed-out field is one continuous lie: no ONSET, no RETURN, no CLEAR, no sound OFF or new ON, and no change to `amp`, `leak_modes`, wander or breath when the seat crosses a hatch. 520	### States and Transitions
521	
522	The Filter has no simulation state machine. These are *presentation-local* machines, none persisted, none in `state_hash`; each is rebuilt from the formula on `hard_start` (PF-33). "Who may cause" names the only actors that can move a machine; the Filter itself never causes a SIM transition.
523	
524	#### S1. Filter service (per client)
525	
526	| State | Entry condition | Exit condition | Behaviour | Who may cause the transition |
527	|---|---|---|---|---|
528	| `COLD` | boot | LOADING begins | no effects; every `perceived` call returns the honest record; the container slot is null | process start |
529	| `HARD_START` | the first RUNNING frame after LOADING; any `force_stage` or `force_level` | one rendered frame later | envelopes set to their targets; every ACTIVE lie drawn at the formula's value for the restored `lie_tau` with full leak; anchors and phases initialised; counter `first_frame_filtered` | Save/Load (LOADING to RUNNING, kernel state); Sanity's QA flags (`force_stage`, `force_level`, SN-28) |
530	| `LIVE` | after `HARD_START` | PAUSED or LOADING | ramps, trajectories, breaths and counters run on their clocks | automatic |
531	| `PAUSED` | kernel pause | resume, or LOADING | `present_time` and the tick are frozen, so every lie clock, ramp, breath, wander and tick freezes; the paused frame still contains every active leak (hue and edge presence do not depend on motion) | the player (pause), the kernel control plane |
532	| `CLEARED` | LOADING, session teardown | `COLD`, then `HARD_START` | presentation-local state (return tracks, slew limiters, envelopes) dropped, never saved | Save/Load, session teardown |
533	
534	#### S2. Stage-bound effect envelope (per viewer, per effect `e` in {rim, bleed, floor}; the class-(c) outline uses `TELL_RAMP_S` in the same form)
535	
536	| State | Condition | Transition | Who may cause |
537	|---|---|---|---|
538	| `OFF` | target 0 and envelope 0 | target > 0 -> `RAMP_UP` | `sanity_view.stage` crossing `STAGE_ENTER` (SIM, instant); for the rim in LIE_BOUND mode (the default) Sanity's `reach_lie_active(P)` becoming true (stage >= 2 and a listed entry with `away` false, `reach_tier` 2 and stepped PENDING to ACTIVE: an ACTIVE lie on a state glyph or lamp-housing glow sprite in the seat's current compartment; a machine-frame lie and any away lie do not drive it; PF-23) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; the bleed never leaves `OFF` while `AMBIENT_FRINGES_ENABLED` is false *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
539	| `RAMP_UP` | envelope below target | slews at the rate latched at the target change (`rate_s`, D.7; at most `1/STAGE_RAMP_S`), so every transition lasts `STAGE_RAMP_S`; reaching target -> `STEADY`; target drops -> `RAMP_DOWN` | the stage, then `present_time` |
540	| `STEADY` | envelope equals target | target changes -> `RAMP_UP` or `RAMP_DOWN` | the stage |
541	| `RAMP_DOWN` | envelope above target | slews at a rate re-latched at the target change (D.7), so it too lasts `STAGE_RAMP_S`; reaching 0 -> `OFF` | the stage (hysteresis exit above `STAGE_ENTER` + `STAGE_HYST` 2000 mSU, after `STAGE_DWELL_RUNS` 25) |
542	
543	The SIM stage steps instantly; the picture arrives like weather. A reversal mid-ramp continues from the current value with its rate re-latched, so the return takes `STAGE_RAMP_S` from any value (D.7). Entering `HARD_START` sets the envelope to its target. The hash `epoch` of the effect increments only in `OFF`.
544	
545	#### S3. Lie presentation (per viewer, per `lie_id`)
546	
547	| State | Condition | Transition | Who may cause |
548	|---|---|---|---|
549	| `NONE` | no entry for the ref and no RETURN in progress, or CLEAR reached after a return (PF-12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | entry appears ACTIVE -> `ONSET` | Sanity (entry appears in `sanity.perception`, SN-16) |
550	| `ONSET` | entry ACTIVE and the departure not complete (`lie_tau` below arrival time) | departure complete -> `HOLD`; entry removed early -> `RETURN` (the follower starts from the in-flight discrepancy) | Sanity (removal: expiry, a falsification, an invalidating re-check, a class disable); sim time (arrival) |
551	| `HOLD` | entry ACTIVE and arrived | entry removed -> `RETURN` | Sanity |
552	| `RETURN` | entry absent and CLEAR not yet reached (CLEAR is the later of discrepancy under `LEAK_EPS_DEG`, gleam amplitude 0 and wander faded to 0; `lie_id` and `lie_kind` stay non-zero throughout; the return is the slew state of PF-13 with the live true value as its target, rate `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | CLEAR -> `NONE`; a new entry on the same ref -> `ONSET` **from its own formula** (discrepancy 0 at `lie_tau` 0); the slew closes the gap from the in-flight value at most `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`, no snap (E-PF-3) | the follower at `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE` (presentation); Sanity (a new entry) |
553	
554	`ONSET` and `HOLD` are both `motion_mode` GLIDE (or TICK or STALE for a readout, or BREATH for a static-pair frame *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*); `RETURN` is `motion_mode` RETURN until CLEAR. SPRITE_SWAP uses the same four states with the gleam-leads-cut onset and the type-split return of PF-19. The leak amplitude follows PF-15 in every state; a stage change never moves the machine.
555	
556	#### S4. Class (c) per subject seat B as seen by viewer A (VS-B; MVP stub)
557	
558	| State | Condition | Draw | Who may cause |
559	|---|---|---|---|
560	| `HUMAN` | `harm_eligible(A)` clear and `tell_on(B)` clear | untouched | SIM (Sanity's flags) |
561	| `TELL` | `tell_on(B)` set (shown to A whatever A's own `tell_on`) | outline fringe ramped in by `TELL_RAMP_S`, breathing | Sanity (`tell_on` of B, `SAN_TELL_ON`/`SAN_TELL_OFF` hysteresis), replicated as `SHARED_SUMMARY` |
562	| `RIG` | `harm_eligible(A)` set | horror rig substituted, hard cut, true position, velocity, beam and voice; the fringe, if `tell_on(B)`, is the single leak fringe | Sanity (`harm_eligible` of A: the actor's own SIM bit, `SAN_HARM_DWELL_RUNS` 150 to set, immediate clear) |
563	| `TELL_AND_RIG` | both | one fringe (SNV-17), never double | both of the above |
564	
565	A is never shown a fringe on A's own body in any state (ART 5.5 read as "never on one's own body"; the own-cone rim fringe sits on the beam rim).
566	
567	#### S5. Mask route
568	
569	| State | Meaning | Transition | Who may cause |
570	|---|---|---|---|
571	| `PER_ELEMENT` (container `NOT_USED`) | MVP: every effect is a per-element material; the container slot is null; not a fault | `CONTAINER_MASKED` after the Vertical Slice spike and its ADR | a project decision (ADR), the pipeline root (slot assignment) |
572	| `CONTAINER_MASKED` | VS-A: a whole-image pass for warm drift on non-anchor content, truth-masked | the mask cannot be exact or allocation fails -> `NONE_C` | the pipeline root; mask availability |
573	| `NONE_C` | fallback: no whole-image pass; per-element only | n/a | mask failure |
574	
575	A null container never reads `NO_MASK` while `filter_route` is `PER_ELEMENT` (PF-25).
576	
577	### Interactions with Other Systems
578	
579	**Reading the tables.** "Names fixed elsewhere" lists the exact hook, mutator, read view, dirty key or block name the counterpart already fixed; the Filter registers **no hook, no mutator and no block** (PF-1), so the hook column is "none" in every row. Each row quotes the counterpart's own Interactions row so bidirectional consistency can be checked; where the counterpart still carries a stale token the row says so and the correction is a *refresh owed* in Cross-References, never an edit made here. "(provisional)" marks every neighbour with no GDD on disk; no GDD file existed when this GDD was written, so everything stated about them is a request this GDD places, to be re-checked when they land.
