#### E. Geometry, safety, ordering and budget

**PF-31. Leak geometry at every ladder step and both passes.**
*Rule.* All fringes, gleams and bands are defined in **art px** and drawn inside the world render at world resolution, never as a post-process on the upscaled container: `n` art px is `n * k` screen px at ladder step `k` (D.10), and the width is always an exact integer multiple of `k` (no sub-art-pixel softness) at **every** `k in [1, k_auto + 2]` (1 to 5 at 1080p, 1 to 8 at 2160p), under render pass A and pass B (pass B takes `k` as a uniform, PIPE:182). Geometry is sampled in texels of the sprite's own texture where possible, so it is pass-agnostic for free; the rim band is sourced from Lighting's four beam-edge mask sprites. A zoom change is a cut (PIPE C6): leak widths are re-derived on the first frame of the new rung and never interpolated across `k`. The drawn marks are sprites or quads, never `draw_line` (4.7 lines lose their antialias feather); no mark is narrower than 1 art px; nearest sampling only; luminance at or below 0.9 x `GLOW_HDR_THRESHOLD`.
*Why.* SNV-29; reflexion: an invariant written against "the default" zoom must be re-checked at every reachable rung. At `k` 1 on 2160p a 2 px band is 2 screen px on a 3840x2160 field: legibility at the Deck is an Open Question (PIPE OQ 4, OQ-PF-4).
*Edge notes.* Character and horror cells keep at least 2 transparent px outside the contour for the outline (target 4 px; the 2-versus-4 reconciliation is the art-director's, 8.2). An outline never covers a sprite pixel (`show_behind_parent`-class).

**PF-32. Flash and photosensitivity: the bound pair.**
*Rule.* The Filter's luminance ramps (gleam, fringe breath, hue bleed, stage envelopes) are not Lighting-originated and do not enter LO-22's governor; the Filter **self-governs by construction**. The binding bound is always the **pair**: PIPE PR-13 (at most `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3 flashes per rolling 1 s, per light, per region of **a ninth of the displayed picture at the current field**, and on the frame mean; a flash is a pair of opposing luminance changes of at least 10 %, red included) **and** HR-13 (no HUD element changes luminance faster than 3 Hz). No full-frame flash on any layer. Every Filter source is amplitude-continuous, **except the rise-only onset step** (0 to `floor_eff` on the first ACTIVE frame, SNV-13: a single-direction change on one gleam element, followed by no fall for at least half a breath period because a lie's gleam breath starts at its trough, D.8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and its modelled opposing-pair magnitude inside any rolling second stays under 10 % at the patch level and far under it at the region level (D.11; the ramps are monotone, the breath is a raised cosine whose turning points are at least 2 s apart), and the verification is a 60 s flash scan at stage 3 at the **largest field** (zoom 1x on 2160p, 36 times the 640x360 area).
*Why.* "Region = a ninth of the displayed picture at the current field" (LO-22) supersedes PIPE D.15's "213x120 fixed" (refresh row 10, X11).
*Edge notes.* Reduce-flashing is a separate toggle from reduced motion; Filter ramps are already flash-free, so it changes nothing here (PF-39).

**PF-33. No clean frame.**
*Rule.* The first RUNNING frame after LOADING, and the first frame after any `force_stage` or `force_level`, is presented **already filtered**: envelopes are set to their targets (`hard_start`), lies are drawn at the formula's value for the restored `lie_tau` with full leak from frame one, and `perceived` is answerable before the first RUNNING frame (Sanity rebuilds `sanity.perception` in `post_restore`, SN-23). No fade-in from clean. Glide and breath *phase* and the slew state may differ after restore; **while a lie is ACTIVE** its presence, kind, leak and displayed value (by PF-11) do not: the first frame shows the formula's value, which equals the pre-save value except for any slew gap that was still closing at the save (D.3), and a return in progress at the save is not restored (the entry had already left `sanity.perception`; E-PF-5). Counter `first_frame_filtered`.
*Why.* "One unfiltered frame would be a free oracle" (SN-23); AC-SL-124: "the first `RUNNING` frame after `LOADING` must already be presented through the Perception Filter for the restored sanity level - the black hold covers any rebuild". This answers SL OQ-11 as co-owner with Sanity and the Pipeline. (orchestrator ruling R20.)

**PF-34. Unseen lies and no leak culling.**
*Rule.* A listed lie is drawn whenever its surface is on screen and lit; there is no "seat away" special case; its trajectory is a function of sim time and reappears at the correct point. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6 GAP; Sanity now lists away entries, SN-23 `away`)* Sanity keeps an entry listed while the seat is in another compartment (`away` true), so a lie seen through an open door, from a hatch or at a zoomed-out field is one continuous lie: no ONSET, no RETURN, no CLEAR, no sound OFF or new ON, and no change to `amp`, `leak_modes`, wander or breath when the seat crosses a hatch. A RETURN begun by a compartment change would give the test "walk out of the room; if the gauge settles it was lying", an end-of-lie signature that PF-G9 and SNV-11 forbid. S3 state and the RETURN follower of a ref that is off screen advance on elapsed `present_time` by scalar arithmetic (no draw or shader work; the follower closes min(gap, R_ret x elapsed)), so a lie that ended while its surface was off screen is, when next drawn, exactly where an on-screen return would have put it (finished unless seen inside its return window); on the first drawn frame after an off-screen interval the ONSET/HOLD slew is re-latched with `hard_start` (D.3) so it equals the formula. At far zoom (the large field) level-of-detail may reduce amplitude *detail* (breath sampling rate only; the wander amplitude and frequency are never reduced, D.4), never remove a leak mode. Counts are bounded by `LIES_MAX`, not by the field, so zooming out multiplies nothing.
*Why.* "A culled leak is an unleaked lie" (OQ-SN-17 answered; SN-15 L-L). (orchestrator ruling R17.)

**PF-35. Frame order and latency.**
*Rule.* In the render callback the Filter runs **after** the Avatar Presenter and **before** Lighting reads the decoy list in the same frame. Dirty-mark in the notification, draw in the render callback (PIPE PR-8). A change in SIM reaches pixels after up to one sanity run (`SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR` 12 ticks = 0.2 s) plus one frame (D.16): stage steps and entry appearance and removal; lies and ramps then evolve on their own clocks.
*Why.* Accepted and stated in Game Feel. (orchestrator ruling R26.)

**PF-36. Anchors that never shift.**
*Rule.* The chest point, beams, character sprites, hand tools, the HUD frame, the true reveal radius and **camera framing (position, zoom, rotation, offset)** are never written. No lie produces a jolt, zoom or shake (a camera jolt from Horror is Horror's and the Pipeline's, not the Filter's). The camera framing joins the never-shift anchor list (art-bible Corollary refresh, row 13).
*Why.* PIPE C1 and C9; PC row 16 ("may never move the chest point (the beam origin under a body substitution)"). (orchestrator ruling R33.)

**PF-37. Presentation randomness.**
*Rule.* Every draw the Filter needs (glide rate and magnitude, wander frequencies and phases, breath cycle periods, tick stagger and sign, mode-drop choice; *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* the GLIDE direction and the numeral mode are published by Sanity and never drawn, PF-13, PF-18) is a **pure integer hash** of `(viewer, ref_key, lie_key, epoch)` plus a per-use tag (D.14), with explicit 32-bit masking after every multiply and operand bounds that avoid dependence on GDScript integer overflow `[UNV]`. Never `rng_derive` (sim-only, KERN D.10, H9), never the global RNG, never `RandomNumberGenerator`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity publishes `lie_id`)* `lie_key` is Sanity's `lie_id` for the lie, masked to 32 bits and forced non-zero (defensive; a conforming `lie_id` is >= 1): `lie_id` is minted from the persisted `next_lie_id` and lives in the saved ledger, so every per-lie draw is restore-exact. **`epoch` is 0 for every per-lie draw**: the epoch is presentation-local and not saved (AC-PF-70), so a per-lie draw that depended on it would change on a restore. `epoch` is used only by the rim, bleed and outline breath envelopes, where it increments only while that effect's amplitude is 0, so a re-draw is invisible (D.14 table). Statistical quality (avalanche, modulo bias) is a test, not an assumption.
*Why.* Restore-exactness and reproducibility across platforms; precedent LO-19 (the pure integer hash for gutter timing). -> ADR candidate: a PRESENTATION-only stream. (orchestrator ruling R19.)

**PF-38. The Never list.**
*Rule.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The Filter never draws (numbered for AC-PF-57b): (1) a sanity meter, bar, ring, number, icon or colour; (2) a vignette or tunnel; (3) blur, chromatic aberration, shake, a scan-line or a glitch; (4) global desaturation or a colour grade; (5) a verdict icon, banner or "you were hallucinating" line; (6) Alarm Red or a "safe" colour in a lie or a debunk; (7) a relief cue on recovery; (8) a self-tell on the player's body; (9) a lie that adds scorch, mist, drip, frost, puddle or sparks; (10) any Attention visual; (11) a phantom in the dark; (12) a phantom that harms, collides, casts light or raises Attention. There is no mastery surface for seam-spotting: no counter of lies spotted, no achievement, no "perception" skill.
*Why.* Guard rails PF-G1 to PF-G5, PF-G9. SL H6: save and pause surfaces are never a hallucination class.

**PF-39. Accessibility semantics per effect.**
*Rule.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Reduced motion:** the glide slows (the **time axis only** is scaled by `RM_GLIDE_SCALE` `[PLACEHOLDER]` 0.7, range 0.7 to 1.0 (raised from 0.6 and 0.5 to 1.0 by the re-review, so that the lie still arrives with at least 10 % of its life to run: `GLIDE_REACH_FRAC / rm_min <= RM_ARRIVE_FRAC_MAX`, D.2), with the rate floor never below 0.3 deg/s, and `D_eff` is unchanged so no lie gets smaller (the worst-case aim distance is the same at every `rm`); the return is scaled by `rm_ret = max(rm, RM_RETURN_FLOOR)` so it takes at most about 1.2 times the normal one) but never rests *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the wander amplitude is never scaled; the lying digit tick survives and is never lowered below `LIE_TICK_MS` (floor 334 ms; it may be raised to 600); the breathing fringe **stays** (it is HR-7's motion channel); honest settle becomes a step and honest tremor may use a held stress mark (Instruments' mechanism). **Reduce flashing:** a separate toggle; Filter ramps are already flash-free. **Colour vision:** the tri-modal redundancy carries it; no global hue remap or daltonization (HR-10). **No sanity-specific setting may remove a leak.** Accessibility Settings exposes only the Filter's published scalars (registry: `filter_accessibility_scalars`: `reduced_motion_glide_pm`, `breath_depth_pm`, `lie_tick_min_ms`) *(provisional — Accessibility Settings, Alpha, undesigned)*; the bounded low-vision hull raise (HR-15) is Lighting's.
*Why.* ART HR-8, HR-10, HR-7; SN-15 L-L. (orchestrator ruling R23.)

**PF-40. Suit readings and the scanner: designed, honest at MVP.**
*Rule.* The HUD asks `perceived(SUIT_KEY(k), viewer)` for the five keys; the Filter returns a wrapped value only when `READING_LIE_STAGE[k]` is at or below the viewer's stage (all "never" in the MVP; designed order `suit.warmth`, then `suit.o2` and `suit.charge`, then `suit.integrity` and `suit.reserve`, SN-19). **Must repeat (verbatim, SE row):** "`true_value` is the only wrap point" on Suit data, and the Filter "may neither remove nor add a body cue, move the chest point, or edit overlay visibility". The scanner is an anchor until `SCANNER_LIE_STAGE` (default never). A lying reading carries the full tri-modal and no suit body cue changes (AC-SE-30).
*Why.* SE-29: "the MVP's single class (b) hallucination lives on ship instruments"; Pillar 2 protects a first-time player's only death clock until the cue ladder is playtested. The flip from honest to wrapped is the Filter's, on Sanity's switch (refresh row 16).

**PF-41. Diagnostics and the Debug Overlay contract.**
*Rule.* The Debug Overlay (DIAGNOSTIC; absent from release builds; never an accessibility feature) calls `true_value` and `perceived` for the **same ref** and shows both with `lie_id`, `lie_kind`, `leak_modes`, `start_run`, `end_run` and `motion_mode`. The Filter publishes counters (registry: `filter_counters`): `lies_drawn`, `leak_modes_dropped`, `leak_repaired`, `lies_partial`, `lie_short_reach`, `lie_unrenderable`, `lie_collisions`, `remote_queries`, `filter_route`, `filter_pass_disabled` (the container state `NOT_USED` is not red), `first_frame_filtered`, `tag_defaults_applied`, `filter_draws_dropped`, `lies_zone_missed`, `render_cpu_us`. `decoy_overflow` is Lighting's. `force_stage` and `force_level` are Sanity's flags (SN-28); the Filter's obligation is to render them with no ramp (PF-33). **Counter severities (confirmed for the Debug Overlay, OQ-DO-2 (iv)):** `lies_partial`, `lie_short_reach`, `lie_unrenderable`, `lies_zone_missed` and `filter_draws_dropped` above 0 are WARN *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; `leak_repaired` above 0 is DEFECT (a malformed entry, already a debug assertion, E-PF-49); `filter_pass_disabled` = `NO_MASK` is DEFECT (`NOT_USED` is not red); `render_cpu_us` is WARN when its median exceeds `CPU_BUDGET_MS`; every other counter (`lies_drawn`, `leak_modes_dropped`, `lie_collisions`, `remote_queries`, `first_frame_filtered`, `tag_defaults_applied`, `filter_route`) is NOTE. **Dev-channel publication (OQ-DO-2 (i), (ii); dev builds only, never read by a release surface):** per lie, `t_return_max`, now the **time to CLEAR** `= max(WANDER_BLEND_S, amp_end / R_AMP, D_MAX_FRAC_ARC x arc_deg / (rm_ret x GLIDE_RETURN_RATE))` with `rm` latched per lie (E-PF-43): 32 s at `rm` 1.0 and 38.4 s at `rm` 0.7 (`rm_ret` 0.83) for the 96-deg cap, against 53.3 s before the reduced-motion return was capped *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; per ref, the PF-45 calibration `(value_lo, value_hi, arc_deg)` (Instruments IW-9 supplies `value_lo` / `value_hi` per quantity). `lie_id` (Sanity's minted `lie_id` verbatim *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*) is kept through RETURN and is 0 once CLEAR is reached (PF-8, OQ-DO-2 (v)) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
*Why.* The index's high risk row ("Per-client divergence is indistinguishable from desync without tooling") is mitigated by contrasting deliberate corruption with real desync; `state_hash` excludes the perceived channel (KERN D.12). (orchestrator ruling R27.)

**PF-42. Budget.**
*Rule.* MVP: **0 container draws** (`D_filter` 0; 1 only if route (a) ships). Leak overlays are counted inside the effects allowance `D_fx` (fringe + hallucination: at most `D_FX_ADDED_MAX` 10 added draws; cited, art bible 8.6, not a placeholder). **The gleam transport is a ladder, tried in this order** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **Planning baseline: no transport is proven** (the engine reference carries nothing on per-instance `CanvasItem` shader parameters, and the MultiMesh path has its own limits: one y-sort position, one texture, one material, one light mask and four custom-data floats per `MultiMeshInstance2D`); spike S-1 therefore runs early as a gating spike, on a backend matrix (D3D12, Vulkan and Compatibility, the renderers the Pipeline supports), before any gleam story is written, and the contingency below is recorded: (1) **instance parameters** on the lying instrument's own material (adds no draw), if spike S-1a (API exists) and S-1b (batching within +1 batch of the baseline) pass; (2) a **`MultiMeshInstance2D` gleam overlay**, one instance per (y-sort depth band, atlas page, light mask) group of lying hosts, so 1 to 6 draws and not "1 to 2 whatever the lie count" (D.12 `G_MM`), if spike S-1c confirms that it batches, orders correctly against occluding sprites at several depths, keeps the gleam lit with its host (mixed light masks) and samples the host's `_msk` edge slice; the instance transform is the host's and the four custom-data floats are packed `r` = `amp` / 1000 (gleam alpha), `g` = the resolved gleam edge in art px / 4, `b` = the index of the host's `_msk` edge slice in a per-atlas slice table / 255 (an instance has one texture), `a` = the surface-kind flags (needle edge, glass, sprite contour) / 255 `[UNV]`; (3) **only if neither fits the budget, that surface is not lied on**: the Filter draws the honest path and counts `lie_unrenderable`, or the host is excluded from `lie_targets.json` at stage 2 (a content rule; the exclusion list is a build lint). **Recorded contingency (reduced lie set, not adopted)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: if neither (1) nor (2) passes on a backend, that backend ships a reduced lie set: only surfaces whose gleam is drawn by their owning node on its own glass (the inspect card, HUD-layer readouts) are lied on, and every world-surface class takes the honest path (`lie_unrenderable`); the fantasy then rests on the card and readout modes, and adopting the reduced set is a decision for the creative-director and the user at the time of the spike result (OQ-PF-43). **A lie is never drawn without its GLEAM** (PF-15). The earlier cut order (drop the housing and glyph gleams, keep the needle's) left palette-silent lies and could not even reach the budget (26 draws less 8 is 18 against 10), and `self_modulate` cannot draw an edge-only gleam, so it is removed from the ladder. The rim fringe adds 1 draw at stage 2 or 3 when it is drawn; the hue bleed is one shared per-sheet parameter (0 draws). The surviving draws per stage on each path are tabulated in D.12. Presentation CPU: at most `CPU_BUDGET_MS` `[PLACEHOLDER]` 0.5 ms median per frame, `CPU_P99_MS` `[PLACEHOLDER]` 1.0 ms at the 99th percentile and `CPU_MAX_MS` `[PLACEHOLDER]` 2.0 ms at the worst frame (D.13), reported by the Debug Overlay *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **MVP GPU row** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the leak block in the shared HullSurface and Emissive ubershader adds at most `GPU_LEAK_REST_MS` `[PLACEHOLDER]` 0.05 ms at 1080p and 0.15 ms at 2160p with every leak parameter at rest, and at most `GPU_LEAK_S3_MS` `[PLACEHOLDER]` 0.15 ms and 0.40 ms at stage 3 with four lies (`[UNV]`; pending spike measurement on RM-DESKTOP / RM-DECK, delegated ruling R12 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)*). Container GPU cost (VS-A) is the Filter's budget, reported separately: target at most 0.4 ms at 1080p and 1.2 ms at 2160p `[PLACEHOLDER]`, measured at the largest field. `STEP_BUDGET_MS` does not apply (no hook). `D_FT_MAX` stays 38 unless route (a) ships (60). The VS-B class-(c) outlines (outline + two beam edges per tell subject) do not fit the 10-draw allowance at three tell subjects and must be re-budgeted (OQ-PF-15).
*Why.* PIPE D.16; ART 8.6. Instance-parameter batching and caps are `[UNV]` (spike S-1, split in three, the scheme of AC-PF-76 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: S-1a, a yes/no editor check that the per-instance parameter API exists on `CanvasItem` in 4.7.2, which needs no reference hardware and is done before the gleam stories; S-1b, instance-parameter batching; S-1c, the MultiMesh overlay, ordering and light-mask test); the budget is stated conditionally rather than as a given. (orchestrator ruling R25, with the draw arithmetic of the systems-designer adopted over the technical-artist's two-overlays-per-lie count.)

**PF-43. Material accounting: no sixth shader source.**
*Rule.* The Filter introduces **no sixth `ShaderMaterial` source** (LO-13 counts five: HullSurface, Emissive, the fringe, per-segment iridescence and the Filter's container slot). The **unlit** family (outline, rim band, decoy rim, lure edge; selected by a uniform integer, not by a render mode) is the existing **fringe** source; the **lit** family (gleam, hue bleed; a dither variant only if OQ-PF-3 adopts it; SPRITE_SWAP frame addressing is not in the block, it is a node frame or region write, PF-19) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* is a default-off include block inside HullSurface and Emissive, driven by a default-zero parameter. A material whose leak parameters are all at their rest values produces output bit-identical to the unmodified material (pass-through exactness). **Never write a material referenced by more than one node** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: a `set_shader_parameter` on the shared HullSurface or Emissive material would put a lie on every instrument that shares it, so the Filter writes only per-instance parameters, the overlay's own material, or a material it created for exactly one node; a unique material per lying host is not a transport (each breaks its batch run, D.12 `B_host`). Build lint PF-6 (vii). Every variant is instantiated once off-screen during LOADING under the black hold, so no first-use compile hitch announces a stage.
*Why.* Whether a shader is lit or unlit is a compile-time property of its source `[UNV]`, so the rulings' "one parametrised leak shader" is read as the fringe source plus an included block (R24 permits "variants of the one parametrised leak shader (or of HullSurface/Emissive)"). This asks HullSurface's owner (Lighting, art) to accept an extra default-off block *(provisional)*; if refused the Filter needs a sixth source and LO-13 reopens (OQ-PF-5).
*Edge notes.* -> ADR candidate: shader-source accounting; material-budget ratification (LO:1344 item 12). Filter shaders are code shaders only (no Visual Shader on a Filter node), read no `TIME` (all phases come from `present_time`), and inherit the sprite's nearest filter.

**PF-44. Fail open to truth.**
*Rule.* If any Filter datum is missing, malformed, unresolvable or throws (a ref with no tag, a calibration record absent, a lie entry for a destroyed subject, an unavailable `true_value`), the affected surface falls back to the **honest path** (displayed equals true, no leak drawn for a lie that cannot be rendered) and the matching counter increments; a Filter fault never propagates to the simulation or to a TRUTH node.
*Why.* The one unrecoverable failure is a lie where the truth belongs; a missing lie is a content bug, a missing truth is a P1 breach. Combined with PF-4 the Filter is fail-safe in both directions of omission.

**PF-45. Dial calibration contract *(designed; PF-45 answered by IW-8, OQ-PF-29)*.**
*Rule.* To draw a lie the Filter needs, per corruptible dial or readout surface, a calibration record supplied by the owning scene through the tag: `arc_deg` (dial sweep), `needle_len_px`, the zone bands as intervals `[z_lo, z_hi]` of the per-mille reading (one for the OK zone, one for the alarm zone) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, and `lsb` (the readout's least-significant unit). Without it the surface is honest (PF-44, `lie_unrenderable`), and the coverage lint (PF-6 vi) makes that a build failure for any kind listed in `lie_targets.json`. Instruments also owe: a pivoted needle as a **separate** sprite or slice, a `_msk` slice naming the glass and needle-edge regions the gleam uses, both honest state frames on one sheet page, and the honest settle applied only when `motion_mode` is HONEST. **Linear branch (K-5, OQ-IW-26).** A LINEAR surface (a tank sight-glass meniscus; Instruments IW-8 `gauge_kind` and D.11 `linear_position`) supplies `travel_px` in place of `arc_deg` and `needle_len_px`. The Filter runs D.2 to D.6 in per-mille space with the angular quantities replaced by Instruments' pixel band (cited, never re-valued here): rate floor `r_floor_pm_s = 1000 x LINEAR_GLIDE_RATE_MIN_PXS / travel_px`; rate ceiling `r_floor_pm_s x GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG / GLIDE_RATE_MIN_DEG` (the dial band's ratio, 4); return rate `r_floor_pm_s x GLIDE_RETURN_RATE / GLIDE_RATE_MIN_DEG`, so D.6's assertion holds; smallest visible departure `D_vis_pm = 1000 x D_VIS_MIN_PX / travel_px`; magnitude cap `D_MAX_FRAC_ARC` of the travel; eligibility `travel_px >= TRAVEL_MIN_PX`. The wander (D.4) moves the meniscus row by `WANDER_AMP_PX`. An ineligible LINEAR surface is not lied on (the honest path, `lie_unrenderable`) unless the ref also has a visible digit mechanism, whose TICK or STALE is then its motion mode (AC-PF-111) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
**Linear column of D.2 and D.3** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the four In-World Instruments constants the linear branch uses are `LINEAR_TRAVEL_PX` 50 (one size at MVP), `D_VIS_MIN_PX` 4, `LINEAR_GLIDE_RATE_MIN_PXS` 0.5 and `TRAVEL_MIN_PX` 40 (all Instruments-owned `[PLACEHOLDER]`, cited in the Cited table, never re-valued here). Every dial quantity that is not already a fraction maps through `arc_deg_ref` 240 (the dial reference of Instruments D.11): `x_pm = 1000 x x_deg / arc_deg_ref`.

| Quantity | Dial (240 deg, 24 px needle) | Linear, `travel_px` 40 | Linear, `travel_px` 50 | Linear form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rate floor | 1.19 deg/s = 4.96 pm/s | 12.5 pm/s (0.5 px/s) | 10 pm/s | `r_floor_pm_s = 1000 x LINEAR_GLIDE_RATE_MIN_PXS / travel_px` |
| rate ceiling (`R_act` at `rm` 1.0) | 2.0 deg/s = 8.33 pm/s | 50 pm/s | 40 pm/s | `4 x r_floor_pm_s` (the dial band's ratio) |
| return rate | 3.0 deg/s = 12.5 pm/s | 75 pm/s | 60 pm/s | `r_floor_pm_s x GLIDE_RETURN_RATE / GLIDE_RATE_MIN_DEG` (6 x) |
| `D_DRAW_MIN` | 24 deg = 100 pm | 100 pm (4.0 px) | 100 pm (5.0 px) | `1000 x D_DRAW_MIN_DEG / arc_deg_ref` (0.10 of the travel) |
| `D_MAX_FRAC_ARC` cap and `DISC_CAP_PM` | 400 pm | 400 pm (16 px) | 400 pm (20 px) | a fraction, unchanged |
| `D_VIS` | 12 deg = 50 pm | 100 pm (4 px) | 80 pm (4 px) | `1000 x D_VIS_MIN_PX / travel_px` |

| `LEAK_EPS` | 0.25 deg = 1.04 pm | 1.04 pm (0.04 px) | 1.04 pm (0.05 px) | `1000 x LEAK_EPS_DEG / arc_deg_ref` |
| `LEAK_D_FULL` | 20 deg = 83.3 pm | 83.3 pm (3.3 px) | 83.3 pm (4.2 px) | `1000 x LEAK_D_FULL_DEG / arc_deg_ref` |
| eligibility | `needle_len_px` >= `NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX` 16 | `travel_px` >= `TRAVEL_MIN_PX` 40 | same | PF-17, E-PF-11 |

The dial's assertion `rm_min x D_DRAW_MIN >= D_VIS` has the linear form of the time condition it stands for, `D_vis_pm / (rm_min x max(r_floor_pm_s, D_DRAW_MIN_pm / (GLIDE_REACH_FRAC x 40 s))) <= GLIDE_REACH_FRAC x 40 s`: at `travel_px` 40, 100 / (0.7 x 12.5) = 11.4 s <= 24 s (the product form would fail, 0.7 x 100 = 70 < 100, because the rate floor, not the draw, sets the slowest rate); the arrival bound `GLIDE_REACH_FRAC / rm_min <= RM_ARRIVE_FRAC_MAX` is unit-free and unchanged. **Worked vector** (`travel_px` 40, FALSE_OK, `L_s` 40 s, hash draw 61): `rate_draw` = 12.5 + 37.5 x 0.061 = 14.79 pm/s, `rate_need` = 400 / (0.6 x 40) = 16.67, `rate_nom` = clamp(16.67, 12.5, 50) = 16.67 pm/s, `D_eff` = min(400, 0.6 x 16.67 x 40 = 400) = 400 pm (16 px), `t_arrive` 24 s at `rm` 1.0 and 34.3 s at `rm` 0.7; the target clamp is [55, 945] pm.
*Why.* The Filter works in per-mille dial space and cannot invent geometry; Sanity's `lie_targets.json` names module surfaces, not dials. Instruments (designed) answers it with IW-8 (`gauge_kind`, the calibration record) and IW-9 (`value_lo` / `value_hi` per quantity).

**PF-46. One live lie per surface.**
*Rule.* If `sanity.perception` holds two entries with the same `subject_ref` for the viewer, the Filter draws the one with the lowest `start_run` only, ties broken by the lowest `lie_id` (matching the Debug Overlay's `(start_run, lie_id)`, OQ-DO-1, AC-DO-38), and only as a last resort by entry order (ascending ledger `slot`, published by Sanity) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity publishes `lie_id`; a defensive fallback only, since Sanity allows one live lie per subject)*; the other contributes no pixels and no sound; counter `lie_collisions`. No leak is lost because the winner carries its own.
*Why.* Sanity's pre-draw gates check immunity, the cap and the gap, not "already lying on this subject". Sanity enforces the invariant "at most one live (PENDING or ACTIVE) lie per (seat, subject_ref)" at its pre-draw gate (SN-16; registry `sanity.ledger`); this tie-break remains as a defensive fallback.

### States and Transitions

The Filter has no simulation state machine. These are *presentation-local* machines, none persisted, none in `state_hash`; each is rebuilt from the formula on `hard_start` (PF-33). "Who may cause" names the only actors that can move a machine; the Filter itself never causes a SIM transition.

#### S1. Filter service (per client)

| State | Entry condition | Exit condition | Behaviour | Who may cause the transition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `COLD` | boot | LOADING begins | no effects; every `perceived` call returns the honest record; the container slot is null | process start |
| `HARD_START` | the first RUNNING frame after LOADING; any `force_stage` or `force_level` | one rendered frame later | envelopes set to their targets; every ACTIVE lie drawn at the formula's value for the restored `lie_tau` with full leak; anchors and phases initialised; counter `first_frame_filtered` | Save/Load (LOADING to RUNNING, kernel state); Sanity's QA flags (`force_stage`, `force_level`, SN-28) |
| `LIVE` | after `HARD_START` | PAUSED or LOADING | ramps, trajectories, breaths and counters run on their clocks | automatic |
| `PAUSED` | kernel pause | resume, or LOADING | `present_time` and the tick are frozen, so every lie clock, ramp, breath, wander and tick freezes; the paused frame still contains every active leak (hue and edge presence do not depend on motion) | the player (pause), the kernel control plane |
| `CLEARED` | LOADING, session teardown | `COLD`, then `HARD_START` | presentation-local state (return tracks, slew limiters, envelopes) dropped, never saved | Save/Load, session teardown |

#### S2. Stage-bound effect envelope (per viewer, per effect `e` in {rim, bleed, floor}; the class-(c) outline uses `TELL_RAMP_S` in the same form)

| State | Condition | Transition | Who may cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OFF` | target 0 and envelope 0 | target > 0 -> `RAMP_UP` | `sanity_view.stage` crossing `STAGE_ENTER` (SIM, instant); for the rim in LIE_BOUND mode (the default) Sanity's `reach_lie_active(P)` becoming true (stage >= 2 and a listed entry with `away` false, `reach_tier` 2 and stepped PENDING to ACTIVE: an ACTIVE lie on a state glyph or lamp-housing glow sprite in the seat's current compartment; a machine-frame lie and any away lie do not drive it; PF-23) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; the bleed never leaves `OFF` while `AMBIENT_FRINGES_ENABLED` is false *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
| `RAMP_UP` | envelope below target | slews at the rate latched at the target change (`rate_s`, D.7; at most `1/STAGE_RAMP_S`), so every transition lasts `STAGE_RAMP_S`; reaching target -> `STEADY`; target drops -> `RAMP_DOWN` | the stage, then `present_time` |
| `STEADY` | envelope equals target | target changes -> `RAMP_UP` or `RAMP_DOWN` | the stage |
| `RAMP_DOWN` | envelope above target | slews at a rate re-latched at the target change (D.7), so it too lasts `STAGE_RAMP_S`; reaching 0 -> `OFF` | the stage (hysteresis exit above `STAGE_ENTER` + `STAGE_HYST` 2000 mSU, after `STAGE_DWELL_RUNS` 25) |

The SIM stage steps instantly; the picture arrives like weather. A reversal mid-ramp continues from the current value with its rate re-latched, so the return takes `STAGE_RAMP_S` from any value (D.7). Entering `HARD_START` sets the envelope to its target. The hash `epoch` of the effect increments only in `OFF`.

#### S3. Lie presentation (per viewer, per `lie_id`)

| State | Condition | Transition | Who may cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NONE` | no entry for the ref and no RETURN in progress, or CLEAR reached after a return (PF-12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | entry appears ACTIVE -> `ONSET` | Sanity (entry appears in `sanity.perception`, SN-16) |
| `ONSET` | entry ACTIVE and the departure not complete (`lie_tau` below arrival time) | departure complete -> `HOLD`; entry removed early -> `RETURN` (the follower starts from the in-flight discrepancy) | Sanity (removal: expiry, a falsification, an invalidating re-check, a class disable); sim time (arrival) |
| `HOLD` | entry ACTIVE and arrived | entry removed -> `RETURN` | Sanity |
| `RETURN` | entry absent and CLEAR not yet reached (CLEAR is the later of discrepancy under `LEAK_EPS_DEG`, gleam amplitude 0 and wander faded to 0; `lie_id` and `lie_kind` stay non-zero throughout; the return is the slew state of PF-13 with the live true value as its target, rate `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | CLEAR -> `NONE`; a new entry on the same ref -> `ONSET` **from its own formula** (discrepancy 0 at `lie_tau` 0); the slew closes the gap from the in-flight value at most `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`, no snap (E-PF-3) | the follower at `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE` (presentation); Sanity (a new entry) |

`ONSET` and `HOLD` are both `motion_mode` GLIDE (or TICK or STALE for a readout, or BREATH for a static-pair frame *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*); `RETURN` is `motion_mode` RETURN until CLEAR. SPRITE_SWAP uses the same four states with the gleam-leads-cut onset and the type-split return of PF-19. The leak amplitude follows PF-15 in every state; a stage change never moves the machine.

#### S4. Class (c) per subject seat B as seen by viewer A (VS-B; MVP stub)

| State | Condition | Draw | Who may cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| `HUMAN` | `harm_eligible(A)` clear and `tell_on(B)` clear | untouched | SIM (Sanity's flags) |
| `TELL` | `tell_on(B)` set (shown to A whatever A's own `tell_on`) | outline fringe ramped in by `TELL_RAMP_S`, breathing | Sanity (`tell_on` of B, `SAN_TELL_ON`/`SAN_TELL_OFF` hysteresis), replicated as `SHARED_SUMMARY` |
| `RIG` | `harm_eligible(A)` set | horror rig substituted, hard cut, true position, velocity, beam and voice; the fringe, if `tell_on(B)`, is the single leak fringe | Sanity (`harm_eligible` of A: the actor's own SIM bit, `SAN_HARM_DWELL_RUNS` 150 to set, immediate clear) |
| `TELL_AND_RIG` | both | one fringe (SNV-17), never double | both of the above |

A is never shown a fringe on A's own body in any state (ART 5.5 read as "never on one's own body"; the own-cone rim fringe sits on the beam rim).

#### S5. Mask route

| State | Meaning | Transition | Who may cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PER_ELEMENT` (container `NOT_USED`) | MVP: every effect is a per-element material; the container slot is null; not a fault | `CONTAINER_MASKED` after the Vertical Slice spike and its ADR | a project decision (ADR), the pipeline root (slot assignment) |
| `CONTAINER_MASKED` | VS-A: a whole-image pass for warm drift on non-anchor content, truth-masked | the mask cannot be exact or allocation fails -> `NONE_C` | the pipeline root; mask availability |
| `NONE_C` | fallback: no whole-image pass; per-element only | n/a | mask failure |

A null container never reads `NO_MASK` while `filter_route` is `PER_ELEMENT` (PF-25).

### Interactions with Other Systems

**Reading the tables.** "Names fixed elsewhere" lists the exact hook, mutator, read view, dirty key or block name the counterpart already fixed; the Filter registers **no hook, no mutator and no block** (PF-1), so the hook column is "none" in every row. Each row quotes the counterpart's own Interactions row so bidirectional consistency can be checked; where the counterpart still carries a stale token the row says so and the correction is a *refresh owed* in Cross-References, never an edit made here. "(provisional)" marks every neighbour with no GDD on disk; no GDD file existed when this GDD was written, so everything stated about them is a request this GDD places, to be re-checked when they land.

312	
313	*Rule.* The entry's disappearance from `sanity.perception` is the **only end signal**; the Filter cannot distinguish the three end types and does not try. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6 GAP; Sanity now lists away entries, SN-23 `away`)* Because Sanity lists every ACTIVE entry of the seat whether or not the seat stands in the subject's compartment, marking it with a bool `away` (SN-23), a disappearance can mean only an end (EXPIRED, DEBUNKED, INVALIDATED); crossing a hatch, a camera pan or a zoom change never removes or adds an entry and never starts ONSET, RETURN or CLEAR. `away` is read by exactly one Filter consumer, the rim gate via `reach_lie_active` (PF-23, D.7 `gate_RIM`); it is an input to no draw, mode, envelope, S3 state, audio request or counter, and a lint (AC-PF-8) fails any other read. A stage change never ends a lie (SN-16).
314	*Edge notes.* The return track is presentation-local: a restore during RETURN shows the true value from the first frame, behind the black hold; no lie is active then, so it is not a clean-frame oracle (E-PF-5). Sanity does not retain ended entries for `LIE_TAIL_S` (OQ-PF-9 answered: ended entries are not retained, loading clears the tail; registry `sanity.perception`), so the tail record and its restore edge are accepted.
315	
316	**PF-13. Glide laws: GLIDE tracks a discrepancy, FALSE_OK and FALSE_FAIL target a zone.**
317	*Rule.* Two laws, each a history-free formula of `(lie_tau, live true value, per-lie constants)` (D.3). **GLIDE** (SN-16 kind) is *delta-tracking*: the displayed value is the live true value plus a signed offset that grows along the glide path at the per-lie rate and then holds, so the discrepancy can neither collapse nor grow unseen between Sanity's 5 Hz re-checks. **FALSE_OK and FALSE_FAIL** are *zone-targeting*: the displayed value departs toward an aim point inside the instrument's OK (or alarm) zone interval at the per-lie rate (the nearest zone point to the true value, pushed `ZONE_MARGIN_PM` inside; success is **the displayed interval, the held value plus the wander, intersecting the zone interval** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*) and then holds the zone, because "OK" is a place on the dial, not an offset; a FALSE_OK that kept tracking a degrading truth would stop hiding it. In both laws the displayed-minus-true discrepancy is 0 at `lie_tau` 0, so there is **no first-frame jump**, and the needle never snaps and never settles. The per-lie **rate** is drawn from the hash (PF-37) inside `[rate_floor, GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG]`, where `GLIDE_RATE_MIN_DEG` 0.5 and `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG` 2.0 are names introduced here, values from ART 7.3 (they are not registry constants), and `rate_floor = max(GLIDE_RATE_MIN_DEG, 28.6 / needle_len_px)`, where 28.6 is `0.5 x 180 / pi` (the rate that moves the needle tip 0.5 art px per second; PF-17; the per-lie rate and magnitude draw is D.2); the **magnitude** is drawn from the hash and then reduced so the departure completes within `GLIDE_REACH_FRAC` `[PLACEHOLDER]` (0.6; range 0.4 to 0.8) of the lie's life; it is capped at `D_MAX_FRAC_ARC` `[PLACEHOLDER]` (0.4; range 0.25 to 0.5) of the dial arc; the dial stop is handled live by clamping the target (D.3), never by shrinking the per-lie magnitude. For FALSE_OK and FALSE_FAIL the magnitude is the cap itself (the needle stops at the zone, D.3), so a zone inside the cap is reachable whenever the life allows (D.2) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity publishes `direction`)* Sanity picks the *kind* and the *direction* (L-D; entry field `direction`: 1 COMFORT, 2 ALARM, stored at the accept and immutable for a `lie_id`, since a changed derivation INVALIDATES the lie, SN-16). The Filter never chooses or re-draws a direction. FALSE_OK implies COMFORT and FALSE_FAIL implies ALARM (zone-targeting; a debug-build assertion checks that the entry agrees); a GLIDE's dial side is `s = d x c_dial` (D.3); the Filter picks only the rate and magnitude (SN-23: WHAT and WHEN, never HOW). Invariant: a GLIDE never moves against its published direction (Sanity's rails L-G, L-W and L-S key on `direction`; a COMFORT-ledger lie drawn toward alarm would visibly push a lethal clock the wrong way). Both laws feed **one slew state per ref**, rate-bounded by `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`, which keeps the needle from snapping after a step in the true value and closes any residual gap (including the in-flight value of a return, PF-14); wander is added outside the slew (D.3, D.4). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The slew is additionally held within `DISC_CAP_PM` of the true value (D.3): a documented, bounded exception to the no-snap rule that stops a truth step or a fast truth ramp (a breach) from leaving the needle a full dial away from the room, which would break the 40 % fairness cap and hide the emergencies `W_MIN_WARNING_S` protects (OQ-PF-40).
318	*Why.* The absolute-anchor alternative (displayed value independent of truth after an anchor angle) carries a restore conflict, because the anchor is presentation-local and the true value may have moved since; the split above needs no anchor. (orchestrator ruling: the systems-designer's two-law form is adopted; the technical-artist's anchor form is rejected for restore-exactness.)
319	*Edge notes.* Build assertion *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `rm_min * D_DRAW_MIN_DEG >= D_VIS_MIN_DEG` (0.7 x 24 = 16.8 >= 12) guarantees that the smallest drawn departure is visible in time even on the slowest reduced-motion time axis (it is the visible-in-time condition `D_VIS_MIN_DEG / (rm_min * rate_need_min) <= GLIDE_REACH_FRAC * 40 s` with `rate_need_min` 1.0 deg/s, D.2). Reduced motion scales the **time axis only**: `D_eff` is the same at every `rm`, so the setting changes when a lie arrives and never how far it can reach. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The claim is worded as a worst-case aim distance and backed by a second assertion: `GLIDE_REACH_FRAC / rm_min <= RM_ARRIVE_FRAC_MAX` (0.6 / 0.7 = 0.857 <= 0.9), i.e. `t_arrive(rm_min) <= 0.9 x L_s` for every lie (a reach-bound lie arrives at `GLIDE_REACH_FRAC x L_s / rm`; the earlier default `rm` 0.6 put every reach-bound FALSE_* lie at or after its expiry, so the setting acted as an easy mode and PF-13's "must reach its zone" failed), which leaves a lie at least `ZONE_DWELL_MIN_S` (4.0 s at the 40 s life) held in its zone. `RM_GLIDE_SCALE` therefore starts at 0.7. The dial stop is handled live: the target is clamped to the dial range minus the wander peak (D.3), so a lie whose truth sits at a stop shows a smaller displayed-minus-true than usual but is still drawn with its gleam, its sound **and its wander, which is the needle's hue-independent motion mode and is never clamped away** (the needle never pins at a stop; a pinned needle rests); counter `lie_short_reach` (once per lie, when the discrepancy is under `D_VIS_MIN_DEG` after arrival time). Such a lie is weak, not unleaked; Sanity's pre-draw gate should refuse a subject whose truth leaves no room (OQ-PF-38). Sanity supplies `first_lie` as a field of the `sanity.perception` entry (registry `sanity.perception`), not inside `params`; the side is implied by the kind for FALSE_* and is Sanity's published `direction` for GLIDE (PF-13, D.3) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* (`params.side` is not needed). The reach of a 40 s lie to a distant comfort zone is a risk owned by Sanity and the art-director (a nearest-edge target or a longer `LIE_LIFE_S` minimum would fix it); counter `lies_partial` measures it (OQ-PF-10). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A FALSE_OK or FALSE_FAIL lie must reach its zone, not merely leave the truth: the Filter's D_eff for these kinds is the cap itself and the aim point sits inside the zone (D.2, D.3); a lie whose displayed interval still misses the zone interval at its arrival time counts `lies_zone_missed`, and the eligibility test belongs in Sanity's pre-draw gate, where the true value and the life `L_s` are known at accept (OQ-PF-38) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the distance to the zone edge plus `m_z` must fit inside the reach the Filter can deliver, `min(D_MAX_FRAC_ARC x arc_deg, GLIDE_REACH_FRAC x GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG x L_s)` (96 deg at 240 deg arc for `L_s` of 80 s or more, 48 deg at 40 s, 200 pm), independent of `rm`, not `D_MAX_FRAC_ARC` alone.
320	
321	**PF-14. Lie end: the glide-return.**
322	*Rule.* On entry removal the Filter starts a return track and moves the displayed value toward the **live** true value at `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE` (`[PLACEHOLDER]`, default 3.0 deg/s; range 2.0 to 8.0; registered; D.6), never overshooting, never settling, never snapping, and tracking the true value at the same bounded rate if it moves meanwhile. It is identical for EXPIRED, INVALIDATED and DEBUNKED (SN-16). The leak amplitude follows the remaining displayed-minus-true discrepancy (PF-15), so there is no separate "lie over" event; the record stays a RETURN record, with `lie_id` and `lie_kind` non-zero, until CLEAR (PF-12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Build assertion: `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE >= GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`.
323	*Why.* SN-16, SNV-11 and P4 ("no verdict"): the end type must never be an oracle. A return slower than the top glide rate would let a debunked needle outlast a live lie, making DEBUNKED a punishment; a much faster return is a legible "the lie just ended".
324	*Edge notes.* Under reduced motion the glide is scaled by `rm` and the return by `rm_ret = max(rm, RM_RETURN_FLOOR)` (`RM_RETURN_FLOOR` `[PLACEHOLDER]` 0.83; range 0.8 to 1.0), which caps the reduced-motion return at about 1.2 times the normal return duration (an unbounded slowdown, 1.43 times at `rm` 0.7, was a hidden difficulty cost and a longer tail that marks an ending); the assertion `rm_ret * GLIDE_RETURN_RATE >= rm * GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG` holds (2.5 >= 1.4 at defaults) (PF-39) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. A new lie on a ref mid-return **starts from its own formula** (discrepancy against the true value is 0 at `lie_tau` 0), never from the return's value, so an ACTIVE lie's displayed value never depends on presentation-local return state. The slew of PF-13 closes the residual gap from the in-flight return value at a rate of at most `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`: no snap, a history-free law, and after a restore the displayed value equals the formula from the first frame (E-PF-3).
325	
326	**PF-15. The leak triple, the ACTIVE floor and the drop rule.**
327	*Rule.* Each lie renders its entry's `leak_modes`: GLEAM (the violet gleam), GLIDE (the motion signature) and SOUND (the sound signature), each sufficient on its own (HR-5). While a lie is ACTIVE its gleam amplitude is never below the stage-indexed floor `floor_eff` (D.5: `AMP_FLOOR_PM` `[PLACEHOLDER]` 400 per mille at stages 0 to 1, falling to `AMP_FLOOR_S3_PM` 250 at stage 3; range 250 to 600) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* even at zero discrepancy, and above that it follows the discrepancy (its rises are instantaneous, its falls are limited to `R_AMP_ACT`, D.5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; after the entry leaves it follows the *remaining* discrepancy from the amplitude at removal, with no step (D.5). The sound request is emitted on the first ACTIVE frame, not when the needle has visibly moved. **Mandatory modes and the drop rule (SN-15 L-L made computable; P1 sane-palette rule).** Two modes are **mandatory on every lie and never droppable**: **GLEAM**, the *palette mode*, because P1 requires that "every hallucination leaks [flesh and violet] somewhere ... Subtle is allowed; absent is not", and a glide or a sound is not a palette leak (a lie drawn with motion and sound but no violet anywhere would be a palette-silent lie); and the **motion mode** (the one mode that survives both hue removal and mute). A lie whose violet is carried by a draw other than the host gleam (a SPRITE_SWAP frame whose gleam leads the cut, a VS-A lure whose flesh or violet content is its own leak, a class-(c) or phantom rig contour with `leak` above 0, E-PF-37) satisfies the palette mode through that draw, and its entry still carries the GLEAM bit. **Only SOUND may be dropped:** at stage 2 or 3, only when the entry carries all three, only when it is not the first lie, chosen by a PRESENTATION-only hash test against `MODE_DROP_PM` and counted in `leak_modes_dropped`. By construction `leak_modes` therefore always contains GLEAM and the motion mode on every ACTIVE lie (`popcount >= 2`, `leak_modes & GLEAM != 0`), at every stage and every level of detail. This is a lint as well as a runtime rule: `lint_leak_palette.gd` (AC-PF-18) fails the build if any lie-content row, fixture or drop-rule branch can produce an ACTIVE lie with `leak_modes & GLEAM == 0`. `MODE_DROP_PM` is `[PLACEHOLDER]` **0 at MVP** (lint) (shipped value; `first_lie` is now supplied).
328	**The invariant, restated: GLEAM plus at least one hue-independent motion mode, on every ACTIVE lie, on every fallback path** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The motion mode is the one that survives hue removal *and* mute, so SOUND never counts as it. Every corruptible surface class has a named motion mode, in the table below; a lie on a surface for which no motion mode can be drawn, or whose gleam cannot be drawn within the budget (PF-42), is **not drawn at all** (the honest path, counter `lie_unrenderable`). The Filter never draws a lie with only part of the pair, so a fallback can reduce how many lies are drawn and never how a drawn lie leaks. `lint_leak_palette.gd` (AC-PF-18) and the fallback lint (AC-PF-108) fail the build for any branch that can.

330	| Surface class | Lie kinds | Hue-independent motion mode (`motion_mode`) | Notes |
331	|---|---|---|---|
332	| Dial gauge needle (GRAPH_NODE, GRAPH_COMPARTMENT, SUIT_KEY dial) | GLIDE, FALSE_OK, FALSE_FAIL | needle drift plus the never-rest wander (record mode GLIDE, or STALE for FALSE_*); the card numeral adds TICK or STALE | the wander runs in every needle lie, including one whose truth sits at a dial stop (D.3 live clamp, E-PF-10); a needle shorter than `NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX` is not lied on unless the ref has a visible digit mechanism (E-PF-11) |
333	| Linear sight-glass | same | meniscus drift plus the wander (PF-45 linear branch) | below `TRAVEL_MIN_PX` not lied on |

335	| State glyph, lamp-housing glow, machine state (static pair) | SPRITE_SWAP; FALSE_OK, FALSE_FAIL on a housing appearance frame | BREATH: the gleam breathes between `floor_eff` (D.5) and `AMP_MAX_PM` over 4 to 6 s (D.8; HR-7 already treats the breath as a fringe's hue-independent channel) | the false frame itself is static; E-PF-12 |

338	*Why.* "Subtle is allowed; absent is not" (ART:73). The earlier draft let the hash choose *which* of the three modes to drop, so a stage-2 or stage-3 lie could have been drawn as glide plus sound with no violet anywhere, breaking the pillar's sane-palette clause (creative-director concern, CD-GDD-ALIGN); the palette mode is now mandatory exactly as the motion mode already was. The stage-2 rim fringe and the stage-3 hue bleed are not relied on to cover a gap, because both are conditional and cuttable. A leak that is a pure function of discrepancy is 0 on the first frame, which would break SN-15 L-L ("the first lie carries all three") and SNV-13 ("full leak from frame one"); the floor closes that onset hole. The `AMP_FLOOR_PM` visibility floor is a sibling of `DECOY_LEAK_ALPHA_PM` 300 and `BREATH_FLOOR_PM` 400 at stages 0 to 2 (the gleam floor is 400 and 325); at stage 3 the user-ruled floor of 250 (D74) deliberately sits below the decoy's 300 (a VS-A overlay, absent at MVP), and the alignment is routed to Lighting and the art-director. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
339	*Edge notes.* A malformed entry with empty `leak_modes`, or with a non-empty `leak_modes` that lacks the GLEAM bit, is a debug-build assertion; release draws GLEAM and GLIDE for the empty entry, **adds GLEAM** to the other, and counts `leak_repaired`, so a palette-silent lie is never drawn (E-PF-49). If audio is muted or unavailable the lie keeps two modes; the player's mute is not a Filter event.
340	
341	**PF-16. The gleam.**
342	*Rule.* Violet `#B07BE6` (never the core `#8A3FD1`), at an **edge only** (glass edge, needle leading edge, housing edge, sprite contour), never a fill or a plane, `GLEAM_EDGE_PX` `[PLACEHOLDER]` (range 1 to 2), set per rung by Instruments' `gleam_edge_px`: 2 art px at k = 1 and 1 art px at k >= 2, so the gleam is at least 2 screen px at every rung (`GLEAM_EDGE_SCREEN_MIN` 2, OQ-IW-4 accepted inside this range). It is drawn on the corruptible element itself, **lit with its host** (it appears only where the instrument is visible; no lit-gate query is needed and none is made, IA-13), and its amplitude is the PF-15 amplitude (breathing on the static-pair classes, D.5). Its transport is the ladder of PF-42 (instance parameters, then a MultiMesh overlay, else the surface is not lied on); a MultiMesh path must keep the gleam lit with its host and sample the host's `_msk` edge slice, which is spike S-1c *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Its peak channel is capped at `LEAK_MAX_CH`, defined **by relation** as `LEAK_MAX_CH := DECOY_MAX_CH` (0.85, itself at most 0.9 x `GLOW_HDR_THRESHOLD`; `DECOY_MAX_CH` is registered and owned by Lighting; `LEAK_MAX_CH` is a name introduced here for the registry stage, not a knob and not a second value), so a leak never blooms (glow is processed before tonemapping since 4.6) and never reads as a light.
343	*Why.* A gleam on an unlit instrument would be a location oracle and would put a phantom in the dark (SN:1267). No flesh tint at MVP (PF-22; ART 4.4 reserves flesh for stage 3 and for surfaces, graded TRUTH_ST, VS-A). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The bleed is ambient by nature (it is bound to no lie), so it ships **default-off** (`AMBIENT_FRINGES_ENABLED` false) as a playtest-gated opt-in (user ruling X11, D76/OQ-PF-2), because ambient violet on pipes contradicts PF-G5 and works as a stage meter. 402	*Why.* Stage 3 is reachable in the MVP only by sustained BREACH or horror contact (SN-29), so it is a late payoff that must not delay the MVP; one shared per-sheet parameter makes the render cost zero extra draws at any zoom, so the real cost is the art channel (OQ-SN-22, user-carried; R29).

405	**PF-25. Mask route and the container slot.**
406	*Rule.* **Route (b) at MVP:** every effect is a per-element material inside the world layer; a TRUTH node never receives one, so truth is exact *by construction*. The Filter publishes `filter_route = PER_ELEMENT` and container state `NOT_USED`, which is distinct from `NO_MASK` and is not red in the Debug Overlay. Route (a) (a second viewport of truth silhouettes multiplied into a container pass) is deferred to the Vertical Slice lighting spike for warm drift; if it ships, `D_FT_MAX` goes 38 -> 60 and fallback C (no pass) applies whenever the mask cannot be exact. There is no `Compositor`/`CompositorEffect` here: that is the 3D post-process path and does not apply to the 2D container slot.
407	*Why.* SNV-29 requires the fringes "be drawn inside the world render at world resolution" (a post-process on the upscaled container would soften the band and break the HD-pixel-art rule); FT OQ 22 requires a per-trail-element mask; the MVP set (gleam, glide, tick, housing, glyph, machine frames, rim, bleed) needs no whole-image pass. 408	*Edge notes.* -> ADR candidate: truth-mask route. A VS-A route (d), a `warm_pm` parameter on the shared hull material instances, is truth-by-construction (an anchor never uses the hull material) but its beam-pixel definition must be settled first (OQ-PF-7). (orchestrator ruling R6, R7.)

410	**PF-26. The decoy list (VS-A; MVP ships the contract and an empty-list stub).**
411	*Rule.* The Filter publishes, per viewer, entries `{decoy_id, kind in {GLOW_EXTENSION, PHANTOM_SHADOW}, anchor, shape, tint_leak, start, end}`. The Filter writes only `CanvasItem` and `Material` members, never a `Light2D` member (PF-2, LO-25); decoys are overlays on mask bit 3 (LO-21, LO-24); warm temperature drift (ART 2.9, VS-A) never recolours a beam pixel (`#FFE2A8`): it is delivered on non-anchor content only or through an exact truth mask (CD-2, LO-25, PF-25).
412	*Why.* Content versus drawing is split so the true reveal radius cannot be moved by a Filter write. (orchestrator ruling R4.)

416	**PF-27. Phantoms, HIDE and lures (VS-A, stubs).**
417	*Rule.* A phantom is a rig that exists only in the viewer's perception, inside a decoy overlay slot, in the lit region only, on walkable tiles only; it has no collision, no light, no Attention input, no footprint and no SIM subject, and never uses `web_strand_*` or `vfx_tell_*`. A HIDE omits a real horror's **body only** (footprints and marks stay). A lure dresses a real junk def with a violet edge and a flesh tint, its edge leak breathing at the same period. The Filter animates; Sanity names intent. A phantom never harms, collides, casts light or raises Attention (PF-G1). Exercised with stubs at MVP. Per HE-40 "the Filter (Vertical Slice) may feed phantom or crewmate-driven poses": the Filter feeds the rig presenter pose streams only for phantoms (VS-A) and for class-(c) substitutions driven by the crewmate's true velocity (PF-29); it never poses a real horror, which Horror poses with `leak` 0; Horror owns the rig asset. Every phantom and every class-(c) render has `leak` above 0 (HE-40, HE:1189; a lint fails any rig instance with no Horror ref and `leak` 0). **Must repeat (Horror's Perception Filter row):** the Filter substitutes or suppresses the rig body only, through the rig presenter `(pose_stream, type_id, leak)`, and never edits marks, L3 state, footprints or audio; marks, disturbances and real positions are TRUTH-tagged and immune; "the hallucination hides the body, never the trail" (HE-32). The decoy criterion AC-LO-32 is discharged here by AC-PF-36.
418	*Why.* SN-22; HE-40. "A shadow with no occluder" remains an unambiguous stage-2 tell because a real horror contributes no occluder (HE-2).

420	**PF-28. Class (c) victim tell (VS-B live; MVP stub).**
421	*Rule.* For every other seat B with `tell_on` (the `SHARED_SUMMARY` flag; `SAN_TELL_ON` 30000 mSU, `SAN_TELL_OFF` 35000, no dwell), every viewer A draws: violet `#B07BE6`, **2 art px outside the Void Steel contour** (fixed by ART 5.5; not a knob), on the full outer silhouette and both edges of the beam cone, on the unlit pass (mask bit 2) so it shows when the subject stands in darkness, casting no light, raising no Attention, silent, breathing 4 to 6 s (PF-30), never flickering, never on one's own body. Set and clear are smoothed by a ramp of `TELL_RAMP_S` (`[PLACEHOLDER]` 8 s; range 6.5 to 15; the floor is the same breath rule as `STAGE_RAMP_S`, D.7; a registry candidate beside `STAGE_RAMP_S`) (the flag has no dwell; the picture does). It is rendered for **every** viewer **including a viewer who is themself `tell_on`**: absence would be a self-sign. The P1 proximity cue is physically real and played by Audio on every client; the Filter supplies only the trigger fact (`tell_on` rising). Web attribution lives in Sanity's `incidents` ring and Scars: **the Filter adds none.** Sprite pixels, beam colour and beam shape are untouched.
422	*Why.* ART 5.5; SN-20; HR-7 (the fringe's breathing motion is the hue-independent channel). (orchestrator ruling R18, R21.)
423	*Edge notes.* Whether the outline is drawn when its subject is unlit is OQ-SH-4 (the shader-specialist recommends lit-only, the art bible says unlit; this GDD follows the art bible and the ruling, and carries the question, OQ-PF-8). **Creative-director recommendation for the OQ-PF-8 resolution: draw it unlit.** Under P4 class (c) "the victim sees a tell": a lit-only outline would let darkness erase the victim's only visual tell, weakening the guard rail exactly where friendly harm is most likely (a monsterised crewmate in an unpowered corridor). The shader-specialist's lit-only suggestion must not win by default.
424	
425	**PF-29. Class (c) monsterised view (VS-B live; MVP stub).**
426	*Rule.* While the **viewer's own** SIM bit `harm_eligible` is set (`SAN_HARM_ENTER` 15000 with `SAN_HARM_DWELL_RUNS` 150; `SAN_HARM_EXIT` 20000; read from SIM, **no PERCEPTION_OUT copy exists**), every other bound seat's body is substituted by a horror rig for that viewer only: a **hard cut within one rendered frame** of the bit setting or clearing (no morph, no half-transformed frame, no pre-eligibility glimpse), the rig at the crewmate's **true position** and driven by the **true velocity**, the **true beam** anchored to the **true chest point** (never re-anchored to the rig), the **true voice**. The substituted rig **always renders with `leak` above 0** (the violet contour, ART 5.5; HE-40 and HE:1189: "any phantom or class (c) render must have `leak` above 0", enforced by a lint that fails any rig instance with no Horror ref and `leak` 0). When `tell_on(B)` also holds for the same crewmate, that contour is the single fringe (SNV-17), never a second one. The Filter sets only Horror's `leak` input and feeds the rig the crewmate's true velocity as its pose stream (HE-40) and the substitution or omission; it never edits pixels, positions, prompts or durations; the prompt key is identical whether the target renders as crewmate or horror (AC-IA-54). Under a body substitution the lightless hand point is free to move for tool placement (PC-11); the chest point never moves (PC row 16).
427	*Why.* Anti-pillar "no intentional PvP": a render substitution gated by a SIM bit, never an attacker option (PF-G2). A flickering pre-eligibility glimpse would reproduce IA-31's leak. (orchestrator ruling R21.)
428	*Edge notes.* The monsterised rig does not draw the held tool's body, while the tool's true emission VFX remain (a free truth channel); this is the recommendation for OQ-SN-26, carried to Horror and the Filter in Open Questions. The prompt a viewer sees on a monsterised crewmate is Interaction's and is identical to the crewmate's (AC-IA-54); the Filter never changes a prompt, a duration or a reach. **Must repeat (Ship Body BDY-30):** the class-(c) rig is drawn at the true position (PC:216); Body has no hallucination field and no per-player variant; the Filter reads Body's SIM read view only and never writes `body.state`.
429	
430	**PF-30. Fringe firewalls and breathing.**
431	*Rule.* The rim and outline fringes are unlit overlays: absent from `emitter.state` (EM-29 lint: no field named `phantom`, `perceived`, `decoy`, `hallucinated`), no Attention input, never reusing `web_strand_*` or `vfx_tell_*` assets or geometry (tangential, continuous, unrooted, per-viewer, breathing versus radial, discrete, rooted, global, beat-locked: AC-SN-154). The Filter never adds, removes, delays or alters a tell cue; **"its anchor list includes the tell cues"** (AT:378 must-repeat). A fringe **breathes**: a raised-cosine amplitude between `BREATH_FLOOR_PM` `[PLACEHOLDER]` 400 (range 250 to 700; it never reaches absent, else the fringe would blink out and be unleaked) and 1000, with a period drawn **per cycle** from the hash inside 4000 to 6000 ms (ART 5.5, HR-7), cycle boundaries at the cosine minimum so a period change never kinks, never locked to `tell_beat`, the alarm sweep (2 to 3 s) or the voice-activity cue; two simultaneous fringes use different hashed periods (D.8). A dead zone of `BREATH_DEADZONE_FRAC` `[PLACEHOLDER]` 0.06 around `2S` and `3S` of every registered periodic source is excluded from the draw; the alarm sweep is registered as `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` (Emitter State; 128 ticks = 2.13 s, range 120 to 180), the single alarm rhythm, so the dead zone has a live input.
432	*Why.* Every legal breath period equals `2S` for some sweep period `S` in 2 to 3 s, so a fixed period locks 2:1 against a fixed sweep (the harmonic finding); per-cycle jitter makes any accidental lock last about one cycle, and the dead zone closes the rest. The sweep is `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS`; Audio's duty is `ALARM_DUTY_MAX_PM` (250) and the pulse leading edge is the contract (Audio CX-A20, F6), so no new constant is needed (OQ-PF-13 closed). Audio D.15 and AC-AA-108 cite `BREATH_LOCK_CEIL` (AC-PF-27) for the `hal` breathing against `tell_beat` and the alarm sweep.
433	*Edge notes.* Breath phase is presentation-local and may differ after restore (SNV-13).

*Rule.* The entry's disappearance from `sanity.perception` is the **only end signal**; the Filter cannot distinguish the three end types and does not try. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6 GAP; Sanity now lists away entries, SN-23 `away`)* Because Sanity lists every ACTIVE entry of the seat whether or not the seat stands in the subject's compartment, marking it with a bool `away` (SN-23), a disappearance can mean only an end (EXPIRED, DEBUNKED, INVALIDATED); crossing a hatch, a camera pan or a zoom change never removes or adds an entry and never starts ONSET, RETURN or CLEAR. `away` is read by exactly one Filter consumer, the rim gate via `reach_lie_active` (PF-23, D.7 `gate_RIM`); it is an input to no draw, mode, envelope, S3 state, audio request or counter, and a lint (AC-PF-8) fails any other read. A stage change never ends a lie (SN-16).
*Edge notes.* The return track is presentation-local: a restore during RETURN shows the true value from the first frame, behind the black hold; no lie is active then, so it is not a clean-frame oracle (E-PF-5). Sanity does not retain ended entries for `LIE_TAIL_S` (OQ-PF-9 answered: ended entries are not retained, loading clears the tail; registry `sanity.perception`), so the tail record and its restore edge are accepted.

**PF-13. Glide laws: GLIDE tracks a discrepancy, FALSE_OK and FALSE_FAIL target a zone.**
*Rule.* Two laws, each a history-free formula of `(lie_tau, live true value, per-lie constants)` (D.3). **GLIDE** (SN-16 kind) is *delta-tracking*: the displayed value is the live true value plus a signed offset that grows along the glide path at the per-lie rate and then holds, so the discrepancy can neither collapse nor grow unseen between Sanity's 5 Hz re-checks. **FALSE_OK and FALSE_FAIL** are *zone-targeting*: the displayed value departs toward an aim point inside the instrument's OK (or alarm) zone interval at the per-lie rate (the nearest zone point to the true value, pushed `ZONE_MARGIN_PM` inside; success is **the displayed interval, the held value plus the wander, intersecting the zone interval** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*) and then holds the zone, because "OK" is a place on the dial, not an offset; a FALSE_OK that kept tracking a degrading truth would stop hiding it. In both laws the displayed-minus-true discrepancy is 0 at `lie_tau` 0, so there is **no first-frame jump**, and the needle never snaps and never settles. The per-lie **rate** is drawn from the hash (PF-37) inside `[rate_floor, GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG]`, where `GLIDE_RATE_MIN_DEG` 0.5 and `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG` 2.0 are names introduced here, values from ART 7.3 (they are not registry constants), and `rate_floor = max(GLIDE_RATE_MIN_DEG, 28.6 / needle_len_px)`, where 28.6 is `0.5 x 180 / pi` (the rate that moves the needle tip 0.5 art px per second; PF-17; the per-lie rate and magnitude draw is D.2); the **magnitude** is drawn from the hash and then reduced so the departure completes within `GLIDE_REACH_FRAC` `[PLACEHOLDER]` (0.6; range 0.4 to 0.8) of the lie's life; it is capped at `D_MAX_FRAC_ARC` `[PLACEHOLDER]` (0.4; range 0.25 to 0.5) of the dial arc; the dial stop is handled live by clamping the target (D.3), never by shrinking the per-lie magnitude. For FALSE_OK and FALSE_FAIL the magnitude is the cap itself (the needle stops at the zone, D.3), so a zone inside the cap is reachable whenever the life allows (D.2) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity publishes `direction`)* Sanity picks the *kind* and the *direction* (L-D; entry field `direction`: 1 COMFORT, 2 ALARM, stored at the accept and immutable for a `lie_id`, since a changed derivation INVALIDATES the lie, SN-16). The Filter never chooses or re-draws a direction. FALSE_OK implies COMFORT and FALSE_FAIL implies ALARM (zone-targeting; a debug-build assertion checks that the entry agrees); a GLIDE's dial side is `s = d x c_dial` (D.3); the Filter picks only the rate and magnitude (SN-23: WHAT and WHEN, never HOW). Invariant: a GLIDE never moves against its published direction (Sanity's rails L-G, L-W and L-S key on `direction`; a COMFORT-ledger lie drawn toward alarm would visibly push a lethal clock the wrong way). Both laws feed **one slew state per ref**, rate-bounded by `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`, which keeps the needle from snapping after a step in the true value and closes any residual gap (including the in-flight value of a return, PF-14); wander is added outside the slew (D.3, D.4). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The slew is additionally held within `DISC_CAP_PM` of the true value (D.3): a documented, bounded exception to the no-snap rule that stops a truth step or a fast truth ramp (a breach) from leaving the needle a full dial away from the room, which would break the 40 % fairness cap and hide the emergencies `W_MIN_WARNING_S` protects (OQ-PF-40).
*Why.* The absolute-anchor alternative (displayed value independent of truth after an anchor angle) carries a restore conflict, because the anchor is presentation-local and the true value may have moved since; the split above needs no anchor. (orchestrator ruling: the systems-designer's two-law form is adopted; the technical-artist's anchor form is rejected for restore-exactness.)
*Edge notes.* Build assertion *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `rm_min * D_DRAW_MIN_DEG >= D_VIS_MIN_DEG` (0.7 x 24 = 16.8 >= 12) guarantees that the smallest drawn departure is visible in time even on the slowest reduced-motion time axis (it is the visible-in-time condition `D_VIS_MIN_DEG / (rm_min * rate_need_min) <= GLIDE_REACH_FRAC * 40 s` with `rate_need_min` 1.0 deg/s, D.2). Reduced motion scales the **time axis only**: `D_eff` is the same at every `rm`, so the setting changes when a lie arrives and never how far it can reach. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The claim is worded as a worst-case aim distance and backed by a second assertion: `GLIDE_REACH_FRAC / rm_min <= RM_ARRIVE_FRAC_MAX` (0.6 / 0.7 = 0.857 <= 0.9), i.e. `t_arrive(rm_min) <= 0.9 x L_s` for every lie (a reach-bound lie arrives at `GLIDE_REACH_FRAC x L_s / rm`; the earlier default `rm` 0.6 put every reach-bound FALSE_* lie at or after its expiry, so the setting acted as an easy mode and PF-13's "must reach its zone" failed), which leaves a lie at least `ZONE_DWELL_MIN_S` (4.0 s at the 40 s life) held in its zone. `RM_GLIDE_SCALE` therefore starts at 0.7. The dial stop is handled live: the target is clamped to the dial range minus the wander peak (D.3), so a lie whose truth sits at a stop shows a smaller displayed-minus-true than usual but is still drawn with its gleam, its sound **and its wander, which is the needle's hue-independent motion mode and is never clamped away** (the needle never pins at a stop; a pinned needle rests); counter `lie_short_reach` (once per lie, when the discrepancy is under `D_VIS_MIN_DEG` after arrival time). Such a lie is weak, not unleaked; Sanity's pre-draw gate should refuse a subject whose truth leaves no room (OQ-PF-38). Sanity supplies `first_lie` as a field of the `sanity.perception` entry (registry `sanity.perception`), not inside `params`; the side is implied by the kind for FALSE_* and is Sanity's published `direction` for GLIDE (PF-13, D.3) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* (`params.side` is not needed). The reach of a 40 s lie to a distant comfort zone is a risk owned by Sanity and the art-director (a nearest-edge target or a longer `LIE_LIFE_S` minimum would fix it); counter `lies_partial` measures it (OQ-PF-10). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A FALSE_OK or FALSE_FAIL lie must reach its zone, not merely leave the truth: the Filter's D_eff for these kinds is the cap itself and the aim point sits inside the zone (D.2, D.3); a lie whose displayed interval still misses the zone interval at its arrival time counts `lies_zone_missed`, and the eligibility test belongs in Sanity's pre-draw gate, where the true value and the life `L_s` are known at accept (OQ-PF-38) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the distance to the zone edge plus `m_z` must fit inside the reach the Filter can deliver, `min(D_MAX_FRAC_ARC x arc_deg, GLIDE_REACH_FRAC x GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG x L_s)` (96 deg at 240 deg arc for `L_s` of 80 s or more, 48 deg at 40 s, 200 pm), independent of `rm`, not `D_MAX_FRAC_ARC` alone.

**PF-14. Lie end: the glide-return.**
*Rule.* On entry removal the Filter starts a return track and moves the displayed value toward the **live** true value at `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE` (`[PLACEHOLDER]`, default 3.0 deg/s; range 2.0 to 8.0; registered; D.6), never overshooting, never settling, never snapping, and tracking the true value at the same bounded rate if it moves meanwhile. It is identical for EXPIRED, INVALIDATED and DEBUNKED (SN-16). The leak amplitude follows the remaining displayed-minus-true discrepancy (PF-15), so there is no separate "lie over" event; the record stays a RETURN record, with `lie_id` and `lie_kind` non-zero, until CLEAR (PF-12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Build assertion: `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE >= GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`.
*Why.* SN-16, SNV-11 and P4 ("no verdict"): the end type must never be an oracle. A return slower than the top glide rate would let a debunked needle outlast a live lie, making DEBUNKED a punishment; a much faster return is a legible "the lie just ended".
*Edge notes.* Under reduced motion the glide is scaled by `rm` and the return by `rm_ret = max(rm, RM_RETURN_FLOOR)` (`RM_RETURN_FLOOR` `[PLACEHOLDER]` 0.83; range 0.8 to 1.0), which caps the reduced-motion return at about 1.2 times the normal return duration (an unbounded slowdown, 1.43 times at `rm` 0.7, was a hidden difficulty cost and a longer tail that marks an ending); the assertion `rm_ret * GLIDE_RETURN_RATE >= rm * GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG` holds (2.5 >= 1.4 at defaults) (PF-39) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. A new lie on a ref mid-return **starts from its own formula** (discrepancy against the true value is 0 at `lie_tau` 0), never from the return's value, so an ACTIVE lie's displayed value never depends on presentation-local return state. The slew of PF-13 closes the residual gap from the in-flight return value at a rate of at most `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`: no snap, a history-free law, and after a restore the displayed value equals the formula from the first frame (E-PF-3).

**PF-15. The leak triple, the ACTIVE floor and the drop rule.**
*Rule.* Each lie renders its entry's `leak_modes`: GLEAM (the violet gleam), GLIDE (the motion signature) and SOUND (the sound signature), each sufficient on its own (HR-5). While a lie is ACTIVE its gleam amplitude is never below the stage-indexed floor `floor_eff` (D.5: `AMP_FLOOR_PM` `[PLACEHOLDER]` 400 per mille at stages 0 to 1, falling to `AMP_FLOOR_S3_PM` 250 at stage 3; range 250 to 600) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* even at zero discrepancy, and above that it follows the discrepancy (its rises are instantaneous, its falls are limited to `R_AMP_ACT`, D.5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; after the entry leaves it follows the *remaining* discrepancy from the amplitude at removal, with no step (D.5). The sound request is emitted on the first ACTIVE frame, not when the needle has visibly moved. **Mandatory modes and the drop rule (SN-15 L-L made computable; P1 sane-palette rule).** Two modes are **mandatory on every lie and never droppable**: **GLEAM**, the *palette mode*, because P1 requires that "every hallucination leaks [flesh and violet] somewhere ... Subtle is allowed; absent is not", and a glide or a sound is not a palette leak (a lie drawn with motion and sound but no violet anywhere would be a palette-silent lie); and the **motion mode** (the one mode that survives both hue removal and mute). A lie whose violet is carried by a draw other than the host gleam (a SPRITE_SWAP frame whose gleam leads the cut, a VS-A lure whose flesh or violet content is its own leak, a class-(c) or phantom rig contour with `leak` above 0, E-PF-37) satisfies the palette mode through that draw, and its entry still carries the GLEAM bit. **Only SOUND may be dropped:** at stage 2 or 3, only when the entry carries all three, only when it is not the first lie, chosen by a PRESENTATION-only hash test against `MODE_DROP_PM` and counted in `leak_modes_dropped`. By construction `leak_modes` therefore always contains GLEAM and the motion mode on every ACTIVE lie (`popcount >= 2`, `leak_modes & GLEAM != 0`), at every stage and every level of detail. This is a lint as well as a runtime rule: `lint_leak_palette.gd` (AC-PF-18) fails the build if any lie-content row, fixture or drop-rule branch can produce an ACTIVE lie with `leak_modes & GLEAM == 0`. `MODE_DROP_PM` is `[PLACEHOLDER]` **0 at MVP** (lint) (shipped value; `first_lie` is now supplied).
**The invariant, restated: GLEAM plus at least one hue-independent motion mode, on every ACTIVE lie, on every fallback path** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The motion mode is the one that survives hue removal *and* mute, so SOUND never counts as it. Every corruptible surface class has a named motion mode, in the table below; a lie on a surface for which no motion mode can be drawn, or whose gleam cannot be drawn within the budget (PF-42), is **not drawn at all** (the honest path, counter `lie_unrenderable`). The Filter never draws a lie with only part of the pair, so a fallback can reduce how many lies are drawn and never how a drawn lie leaks. `lint_leak_palette.gd` (AC-PF-18) and the fallback lint (AC-PF-108) fail the build for any branch that can.

| Surface class | Lie kinds | Hue-independent motion mode (`motion_mode`) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dial gauge needle (GRAPH_NODE, GRAPH_COMPARTMENT, SUIT_KEY dial) | GLIDE, FALSE_OK, FALSE_FAIL | needle drift plus the never-rest wander (record mode GLIDE, or STALE for FALSE_*); the card numeral adds TICK or STALE | the wander runs in every needle lie, including one whose truth sits at a dial stop (D.3 live clamp, E-PF-10); a needle shorter than `NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX` is not lied on unless the ref has a visible digit mechanism (E-PF-11) |
| Linear sight-glass | same | meniscus drift plus the wander (PF-45 linear branch) | below `TRAVEL_MIN_PX` not lied on |
| Numeral-only readout (digit mechanism, no needle) | GLIDE; FALSE_OK, FALSE_FAIL | TICK for GLIDE; for FALSE_* STALE **plus the gleam breath** (a held digit alone is not motion, so the record carries BREATH's gleam modulation) | D.9 |
| State glyph, lamp-housing glow, machine state (static pair) | SPRITE_SWAP; FALSE_OK, FALSE_FAIL on a housing appearance frame | BREATH: the gleam breathes between `floor_eff` (D.5) and `AMP_MAX_PM` over 4 to 6 s (D.8; HR-7 already treats the breath as a fringe's hue-independent channel) | the false frame itself is static; E-PF-12 |
